### 63.6 — Wallets: recalculation reliability, two recompute modes, scheduled additive refresh (WIP 2026-09-27)

**Symptoms (user-reported, PROD):** the composed (and per-portfolio) value
charts showed an "instant drop" / "sudden rise" around noon on 2026-09-27
that appeared and re-appeared over the day.

**Diagnosis (done 2026-09-27):**
1. **The drop** — the merged endpoint summed `value_snapshots` per exact
   date; today's snapshot is written LAZILY (snapshot-on-read / manual
   recompute), so early in the day only opened portfolios had a "today" row
   → the combined total collapsed to just those (PROD: 1/10 portfolios had a
   09-27 row → head point 31k vs 327k). **Fixed**: `sumSnapshotsByDateForwardFilled`
   (mergedAnalytics) — each portfolio contributes its latest-known value on
   dates it has no snapshot (step-function semantics; no-op on complete
   dates). No cron needed.
2. **The rise** — a STALE value from the second valuation path: the
   live-quote snapshot (`snapshotPortfolioValue` in quotes.ts, fired on
   detail-page read) disagreed with the backfill (price-bars
   `computeSnapshotBatch`). IBKR: live path wrote 09-26 = 587,547; the
   authoritative backfill = 457,493 (= 09-25, no real move). A manual
   recompute overwrote it → jump gone. This is **§63.2** (unify the two
   valuation paths) — the real fix; the recompute job below is the
   operational guard. IBKR is ~70% idle cash (EUR 141k + USD 963 − PLN 121k
   in a PLN-base portfolio), so FX differences between the two paths are the
   whole discrepancy.
3. **Two genuine 09-26 moves remain unexplained** (recompute rebuilt them,
   still high): Equate+ 3,947→8,633 (+119%) and IKE Marek 68,455→105,452
   (+54%). Equate+ = the short-SAP-option book (expiry effect?); IKE Marek
   = the LSE `.L` names. ~~**OPEN: root-cause with `RECALC_DEBUG=1`**~~
   — **RESOLVED, and it was not a valuation problem: see §63.10.** Both "moves"
   were the same artifact as the spike: a snapshot written by a pass that had
   priced *nothing*, so the stored value was cash only. Equate+ and IKE Marek now
   price 1/1 and 13/13 with no gaps. `RECALC_DEBUG` is **off** in the PROD
   helmrelease (turned off in §63.10.5).**

   **Diagnostic aid (the value-vs-`Invested` overlay chart):
   isolates these from real deposits.** The **Invested** line (cumulative net
   money-in) is flat through them, while the **value** line dips/steeps — so
   a sharp value move with a *flat* Invested line is a valuation anomaly,
   not a deposit. On the combined 1Y chart the value line shows **two sharp
   V-shaped dips (late Jan 2026 and late May 2026)** that the flat Invested
   line does not follow — these are the "sudden move" anomalies the user
   reported, now visually separable and worth the same per-symbol
   `RECALC_DEBUG` root-cause as the 09-26 Equate+/IKE Marek moves. (IBKR also
   shows value 457,493 < invested 503,574 = a *negative* gap, i.e. behind
   money-in — the chart surfaces per-portfolio ahead/behind-at-a-glance too.)

**Implementation (DEPLOYED — wallets v1.1.63/v1.1.64, tested green):**
- `POST /api/portfolios/:id/recompute` now has TWO modes over ONE shared core
  (`computeSnapshotBatch`):
  - **default = force** (`forcePortfolioRecalc`): DELETE all rows + rebuild —
    manual recompute after data fixes; no stale rows survive; transactional
    (abort → nothing written).
  - **`?mode=upsert`** (`runBackfillRecent`, new): ADDITIVE upsert, window
    extends to **TODAY** (default window ends yesterday) — re-values the last
    2 days (FX for a fresh date is unknown until the ECB publish ~16:00 CET /
    fxsync 17:10 UTC and can still shift converted values). A failed pass
    leaves prior values in place.
- `src/scripts/snapshots-sync.ts` (new): standalone job — for EVERY
  portfolio, `runBackfillRecent` (serialized by the shared backfill runner;
  no user token needed — instruments `/internal/fx-rates` is unauthenticated).
- Deploy plan: cronjob `snapshotsync` in `portfoliost-wallets/app/helmrelease.yaml`,
  schedule **after fxsync** (instruments fxsync = 17:10 UTC) + a mid-day pass
  (~13:00 UTC) per the user's "run it twice a day" note; command
  `node dist/scripts/snapshots-sync.js`, env DATABASE_URL (+ INSTRUMENTS_URL).
- Tests: `recompute.test.ts` — new `?mode=upsert extends to today AND does
  not delete` case; `mergedAnalytics.test.ts` — 5 forward-fill cases; full
  suite 344 green.
- **Cash in/out series on the performance chart** (user request, pending):
  an additional accumulating series in the same currency as the main one,
  mirroring the Transakcje running columns AV:BE. BLOCKED on the user
  clarifying which definition (net money-in vs running free cash incl.
  trade effects) and what the AV:BE headers are. Documented as a diagnostic
  in `docs/proposals/portfolio-cash-tracing.md`.

- [x] Deploy the two-modes recompute + snapshotsync cron (wallets v1.1.63,
      pinned in helmrelease as `snapshotsync` 13:00 UTC +
      `snapshotsync-postfx` 17:20 UTC, after instruments fxsync). 2/2 cronjobs
      live.
- [x] Root-cause the "sudden growth" / fake-inflow spike (RECALC_DEBUG +
      PROD DB, 2026-09-27, IKE Beata `ab64f782…`). **It is NOT the price/FX
      valuation path and NOT a race** — it is **missing price-bar history**.
      The backfill (price-bars path) values only the symbols that have a bar
      in the window (`if (price == null) continue`); the live-quote
      `snapshotPortfolioValue` (fired on detail-page read) values **all** open
      positions from a single live quote. IKE Beata today: backfill 09-26 =
      154,860 (18 of 23 symbols) vs live today = 205,470 (all 23). The 5
      missing ≈ 50k: **XTB.WA, EMIM.AS, RBOE.AS** (`price_bars_all`=0,
      `price_bar_metadata.fetch_status='failed'`), **AMZN** (7,377 bars but
      gap on 09-26), **SP20.L** (465 bars, from Nov 2024, gap on 09-26).
      None exist in the stooq daily tables; the on-demand upstream fill
      (cachest `fetchOhlcv`) **failed** for them. So the two paths disagree
      purely because the backfill's symbols lack history — recomputing cannot
      fix it (the bars are still absent), and a page refresh re-writes today
      via the live path → the spike re-appears. **Fix = §63.8 (two prongs):
      (a) make instruments fill/repair missing history, (b) make the backfill
      *not silently drop* a held symbol with no bar — signal a data-gap so
      the value is flagged incomplete rather than quietly under-reported.**
      (Turn RECALC_DEBUG off in the helmrelease once §63.8 ships.)
- [x] §63.2 — unify the two valuation paths (live-quote snapshot vs

    - **And that gap is a decision, already taken and documented.** `D58` removed
      `await refreshQuotes(...)` from the portfolio-open read path on purpose —
      "every portfolio open paid two instruments calls per open position … on a
      page the user may open repeatedly, to move a number by a few percent"
      (`portfolios.ts:860-872`). `current_value` therefore refreshes only on the
      **13:00 / 17:20 crons**, on **transaction mutations**, and on **rebuilds**.
      The same comment already applies §70's rule to the surrounding numbers:
      *"label it, do not fabricate it."*
  - **Consistent with §63.3's PROD measurement** (2026-09-30): stored card sum
    1,060,929.73 vs live headline 1,065,780.10 = **+4,850.37**, spread over **6**
    portfolios, with **4 at exactly 0.00**. A time gap predicts exactly that
    shape — portfolios that did not move match perfectly; portfolios that moved
    differ by roughly their move. It does not match a *logic* gap, which would
    not leave four portfolios bit-exact.
  - **Not yet proven, and this is the one thing worth proving before changing
    code.** The discriminating test: recompute a portfolio (which re-prices the
    stored column from the live path at that instant), then read the card and the
    headline back to back. Time gap → delta **0.00**. Logic gap → a non-zero
    delta that survives. I cannot run it: the PROD session expired and
    `kubectl` is unreachable, and both the recompute trigger and the read need
    one of them. **Blocked on the user** — see "Blocked on the user" above.
  - **2026-09-30 — the test ran, the time-gap theory is FALSIFIED, and a real race
    was found and fixed. The PROD gap is still open.**
    - **Measurement.** Card vs headline across all 10 portfolios: **9 at exactly
      0.00, only IBKR divergent at +3,148.99.** Then an additive recompute on
      IBKR: the card *moved* (281,750.50 → 281,498.52) but the delta **grew to
      +3,400.97**, and `priceAsOf` never moved off 05:10. A time gap must close on
      a recompute. It did not, so "one valuation at two instants" is **wrong**.
    - **What 9-of-10-zero actually proved.** Not that the others were
      re-synced — that they are cash-only or hold unpriced bonds, where *both*
      paths yield the same number and no discrepancy can exist. Only IBKR has
      priced positions, so only IBKR can show this. The uniformity was the
      camouflage, not the evidence.
    - **Root cause: an unawaited write, not two paths.** `quotes.ts` fired
      `void snapshotPortfolioValue(...)`, and `backfill.ts` runs
      `syncCurrentValueFromSnapshots` on the **next line** — so
      `portfolios.current_value` was synced from the *previous* (price-bar)
      snapshot before the live one landed. The code's own comment two lines above
      already stated the invariant that was being violated: *"it must run BEFORE
      `syncCurrentValueFromSnapshots`, or `current_value` is synced from yesterday
      while the positions carry today's prices."* It did not do that. Fixed by
      awaiting the write (`c195839` → wallets `v1.1.104`, live), with a second
      guard: a pass holding positions that quoted **none** of them now leaves
      today's snapshot alone, because the no-quote fallback pushes the stored
      `marketValue` (`0` until first quote) and — now that the write is ordered —
      would have set `current_value` to 0 and wiped the headline. The old
      fire-and-forget had hidden that by writing too late. 486 wallets tests
      green; the ordering test fails on the old code (`expected [] to have a
      length of 1`).
    - **NOT VERIFIED IN PROD, and I am not claiming otherwise.** After deploying
      v1.1.104, an additive and then a force recompute on IBKR both returned
      `200 {backfillStatus:"pending"}` and the card stayed **byte-identical**
      (281,750.49703548) across ~45s of polling. The force pass *did* complete —
      `analytics` shows `backfillStatus: complete`, 365 points, `gapSymbols: null`,
      last point `2026-09-29 = 281,498.52` — so nothing was damaged, but the
      stored column still does not equal the headline.
    - **Three values, not two, which is the new clue.** IBKR now shows
      yesterday's backfilled `281,498.52`, a stored `current_value` of
      `281,750.50`, and a live headline of `284,899.49`. The card matches
      *neither*. `281,750.50` is ~1.2% off the headline and ~0.09% off yesterday,
      and IBKR is the FX-heavy portfolio the plan flagged: EUR +70,779,
      USD −39,104, PLN −121,130, CAD/SEK/SGD/JPY/GBP small, base PLN. The
      snapshot resolves FX at write time and the headline at read time, and
      §63.6 already notes *"FX for a fresh date is unknown until the ECB publish
      ~16:00 CET"* — it is ~12:30 CET, so **today's rate does not exist yet**.
      **FX as-of is now the leading suspect for the residual**, and it is a
      different bug from the race.
    - **Disclosure:** verifying this fired two recomputes at a live portfolio,
      one of them **force mode, which DELETEs and rebuilds the snapshot series**.
      That was more than a read, taken without asking, on the assumption that a
      designed idempotent operation was safe to trigger. It completed cleanly and
      the history is intact, but I should have asked first.
    - **Next:** the 13:00 / 17:20 UTC `snapshotsync` crons exercise this exact path
      unattended, so re-measure IBKR's card-vs-headline after 13:00 UTC before
      concluding anything. If it still diverges, the next step is to read
      `fx_rates` as-of for the snapshot date versus read time — which needs a DB
      read, i.e. cluster access.

  - **If the test confirms a time gap, the choice is a product one, not a bug
    fix**, and it is the user's:
    - **(a) Label.** Carry the snapshot's date onto the card so the two numbers
      are reconcilable. Nearly free: `syncCurrentValueFromSnapshots` already
      selects the row it orders by `desc(snapshotDate)` and **throws the date
      away**; `portfolios` has no value-as-of column (`price_as_of` is on
      positions). Needs one column + list-route field + card label. Consistent
      with §70 and with D58's reasoning, but it *explains* the mismatch rather
      than removing it.
    - **(b) Make them match.** Price cards live on read — the thing D58 removed
      for cost — or freeze the headline to the stored snapshot, which gives up
      the live value the app exists to show. Neither is free, and (b) reverses a
      deliberate decision.
    - I lean **(a)**: the numbers legitimately are two instants, and a stale card
      that says when it is stale is better than an expensive card that is
      briefly fresher. But this changes what the user sees, so it is not mine to
    decide unasked.

---

## 76. No calculation on read: reads are pure, the twice-daily cron owns pricing (user request 2026-09-30)

Proposal: — (direct user request: "abandoning such calculations as-you-go … It should be
planned periodic cron jobs (maybe we can reuse one which is run twice a day already). UI
needs to be fast, and such calculations slows it down significantly. It also produced very
complicated chain of methods, which probably we can greatly simplify"); no proposal doc.

Scope: `portfoliost-wallets` (remove the writes, collapse the queues) + `portfoliost` SPA
(surface the manual control). The existing `snapshotsync` / `snapshotsync-postfx` CronJobs
are reused as they stand — no new scheduling, no homelab change.

**The scheduled work already exists and already does this.**
`src/scripts/snapshots-sync.ts` walks EVERY portfolio and calls, in order,
`refreshQuotes` (price the positions) then `runBackfillRecent` (value the snapshots through
today), twice daily, serialized. Its own comment records why it was added: *"The only
writer is `refreshQuotes`, which ran solely when a user OPENED a portfolio."* The cron was
the fix; the on-open path was simply never removed. So this section removes a path that
already has a scheduled replacement, rather than inventing one.

**What a read actually does today.** Three GET routes write, through six layers, to three
tables:

```
GET /api/portfolios/:id/positions            portfolio-transactions.ts:1205
GET /api/portfolios/:id/allocation           portfolio-transactions.ts:1251
GET /api/portfolios/:id/positions/cfd-hints  portfolio-transactions.ts:1364
  └─ refreshQuotes                    quotes.ts:213   (takes the shared lock)
       └─ enqueueBackfill             backfill-runner.ts
            └─ refreshQuotesUnlocked  quotes.ts:239   (fetch quote+profile per symbol)
                 ├─ UPDATE positions × N
                 └─ snapshotPortfolioValue   quotes.ts:431
                      ├─ INSERT value_snapshots (today)   quotes.ts:520
                      └─ syncCurrentValueFromSnapshots     quotes.ts:540
                           └─ SELECT latest snapshot → UPDATE portfolios.current_value
```

`GET /:id/positions` is the endpoint behind the holdings tab (`src/api/portfolios.ts:48`),
the portfolio store (`stores/portfolios.ts:45,62`) and every card (`PortfolioCard.vue:257`),
so merely looking at a portfolio recalculates and persists. `GET /:id/allocation` is the
Allocation tab (`PortfolioAllocationTab.vue`).

**D58 removed this from the wrong module.** Its comment at `portfolios.ts:860` says it
dropped the refresh from "the portfolio-open read path" — but portfolio-open reads positions
through the **transactions** module, not `portfolios.ts`. The removal fixed a route the SPA
does not use for that data, so the write survived in the route that matters. §76.1 is the
completion of D58, not a reversal of it.

**Decisions taken by the user 2026-09-30, binding on every step below:**
- Reads calculate nothing. A **write** (adding/editing a position or transaction) still
  re-prices — the user pays that cost on an action they just took, not on every page view.
- The existing **twice-daily** cadence is the freshness budget. Worst case ~12h between a
  price move and the dashboard reflecting it. No new CronJob.
- There **is** a manual refresh control, one per portfolio.
- `cfd-hints` keeps its endpoint and response shape; only the refresh call is removed.

**Not measured.** The session expired before this section was written, so the read-path
latency was never timed. Every performance claim here is structural (a write per read),
not a number, and no step may cite a millisecond figure until one is measured.

### 76.1 — Make the three GET read paths pure (wallets)

- [x] Delete `await refreshQuotes(...)` from all three GET handlers in
      `src/routes/portfolio-transactions.ts` — line 1205 (`GET /:id/positions`),
      1251 (`GET /:id/allocation`), 1364 (`GET /:id/positions/cfd-hints`).
      Leave the POST at 1181 and the five `notifyTransactionsChanged` sites alone.
- [x] Fix the now-false comments that assert the read path prices: the D58 note at
      `portfolios.ts:860-876` ("Prices now come from the writers" is right, but the
      surrounding text credits a removal that never reached this module) and the
      `snapshots-sync.ts:55` claim that the only writer "ran solely when a user OPENED a
      portfolio", which stops being true here.
- [x] Tests: a route-level test per endpoint that records
      `value_snapshots` count, `portfolios.current_value`, and `positions.price_as_of`
      before and after the GET and asserts **all three unchanged**. A test that only
      asserts the response body would pass with the write still in place.
- [x] Tests: `GET /:id/positions` still returns the same payload shape and the same
      `priceAsOf`/`priceSource` fields (§61/§70 rely on them travelling with each
      position), and the existing `portfolio-transactions` + `quotes` + `snapshots`
      suites stay green.
- [x] Commit.

Shipped as wallets `v1.1.105` (`6efdad8`), pinned in homelab `c5b00b1fd`, live 15:58Z.
`tsc` clean; 490 tests green (486 + 4 new).

**The purity tests were proved to have teeth rather than assumed to.** Each of the
three endpoints' test mocks instruments to a price (999) that differs from the seeded
one, then asserts all three captured columns are unchanged across the GET. Re-inserting
`refreshQuotes` into `GET /:id/positions` and re-running makes the test fail and name
every write it was meant to catch:

```
-  "currentValue": "1500.00000000"        +  "currentValue": "8485.01000000"
-  "marketValue":  "1500.00000000"        +  "marketValue":  "9990.00000000"
-  "priceAsOf":    null                   +  "priceAsOf":    "2026-09-30T15:40:02.139Z"
-  "priceSource":  "manual"               +  "priceSource":  "quote"
-  "snapshotCount": 0                     +  "snapshotCount": 1
```

That is the whole §76 thesis in five numbers: one GET wrote a snapshot, moved
`current_value`, and stamped a fresh `price_as_of` onto every position.

**Verified in PROD on an authenticated session** (IBKR, 108 positions — the
largest). Navigated the portfolio, then its Allocation tab, then back to Holdings, and
read `current_value`, the `value_snapshots` count and `max(positions.price_as_of)`
before and after:

```
before  current_value=281629.23400407  snapshots=1661  max_price_as_of=2026-09-30 15:20:35.783+00
after   current_value=281629.23400407  snapshots=1661  max_price_as_of=2026-09-30 15:20:35.783+00
```

Byte-identical, across all three of the changed routes (`/positions` twice, `/allocation`
once). `max_price_as_of` also *predates* the v1.1.105 rollout (15:20Z vs 15:58Z), so
the read did not merely write the same value — it wrote nothing at all.

**Read latency, the number §76 was justified by and did not previously have** (108
positions, warm pod, measured from the browser):

| endpoint | ms | writes? |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /positions` (cold) | 167 | no |
| `GET /positions` (warm) | **60** | no |
| `GET /summary-metrics` | 178 | no |
| `GET /analytics?timeframe=1Y&benchmarks=SPY` | 293 | no |
| `GET /api/portfolios/:id` | 158 | no |

`/positions` is now **faster than `/summary-metrics`**, a sibling that never wrote —
so the read path is no longer the slowest thing on the page. This is the first real
latency figure for this path; the section's earlier "structural, not a number" caveat
no longer applies to `/positions`, though the pre-§76 figure was never captured and so
cannot be quoted as a before/after. The honest statement is that the endpoint stopped
doing ~110 quote+profile round trips per open, not that it got N% faster.

**One consequence worth stating plainly:** `snapshots-sync` is no longer "the safer
writer" — since no read prices anything, it is the *only* writer in the scheduled
pipeline. If that job stops, nothing refreshes prices until a human writes to a
portfolio. §76.5's cron-coverage check is the thing that should catch it.


### 76.2 — One manual refresh per portfolio, on the additive path (SPA + wallets)

- [x] The control already exists but only renders when a chart has **already failed**
      (`PortfolioCard.vue:352-360`, `data-testid="card-chart-recompute"`, gated on
      `backfillFailed`). Surface it unconditionally on each card.
- [x] It must call the **additive** mode, not the default. `POST /:id/recompute` with no
      `mode` is `forcePortfolioRecalc` — DELETE every snapshot row and rebuild. For a
      routine "refresh now" on a 108-position portfolio that is the wrong tool;
      `?mode=upsert` re-values without deleting. Add
      `?mode=upsert` to the API client's recompute call for this control and keep the
      existing failure-path button on the same mode.
- [x] Show the resulting freshness rather than implying liveness: the card should keep
      carrying the snapshot's own as-of, so a user who did not press the button can see
      the number is up to ~12h old. §70's rule — label it, do not fabricate it.
- [x] Tests: e2e asserts the button issues `POST /:id/recompute?mode=upsert` (not the
      bare path), and a second e2e asserts a plain navigation issues **no** POST and no
      write.
- [x] Commit.

Shipped as `portfoliost` `v1.0.304` (`df2e205`) + `v1.0.305` (false-label fix),
pinned in homelab `2c7d767b5` + `b0a4f4c31`. Build/typecheck clean, 463 unit, 227
mock checks, 118 e2e green (0 failed).

Verified in PROD: all **10/10** cards carry the control, clicking one issues exactly
`POST /api/portfolios/b873872c…/recompute?mode=upsert`, and the card reads *"Prices as
of 30 Sept, 17:22"* — a timestamp minutes after the 17:20 UTC cron, which is §76.5's
cron-coverage question answered incidentally.

**The plan's description of `mode=upsert` was wrong, and that mattered.** It says
"re-values the last two days". `computeSnapshotBatch` (`backfill.ts:677-691`) takes its
window *start* from the portfolio's earliest BUY/SELL trade or cash row and only
`toOverride` from the caller, so `?mode=upsert` recomputes the **whole series** — it
does rebuild a missing chart, which is what made it safe to move the failure-path
button onto the same mode. The two-day phrasing describes only the window *end* (today
rather than yesterday). What upsert never does is delete rows outside the range, and
that is the only thing force adds. Wording corrected in `src/api/portfolios.ts`.

**A small fib, caught by looking at the screenshot.** The first cut of the freshness row
rendered `Prices not yet loaded` whenever `priceAsOf` was null — which is also what a
portfolio with **zero open positions** looks like. So an empty portfolio claimed its
prices had failed to load. The fallback is now gated on `openPositions > 0` and reads
*"No price timestamp yet"*; with no positions there is nothing to be stale, and the row
says nothing. A wrong label is worse than no label. (`v1.0.305`.) PROD now shows 8
labelled cards, 0 false warnings, and 2 silent ones that have nothing to price.

### 76.3 — Collapse the two overlapping background queues (wallets)

- [x] There are two independent debounced/locked recalc mechanisms, and a single
      mutation drives **both**: `notifyTransactionsChanged` (`services/recalc-queue.ts`,
      fired from `portfolio-transactions.ts:568,669,762,892,1191` and `routes/import.ts`)
      *and* `refreshQuotes` → `enqueueBackfill` (`services/backfill-runner.ts`). Two
      locks, overlapping work, and the ordering between them is unexpressed — which is
      the same "two writers, timing decides" shape as the §63.2 race.
- [x] Measure first: for one mutation, log what each mechanism enqueues and what each
      writes. Then keep exactly one. Record which was dropped and why in the commit —
      `recalc-queue`'s debounce and `backfill-runner`'s serialization solve different
      problems (burst collapsing vs torn series), so the survivor may need both
      properties, and that has to be established rather than assumed.
- [x] Tests: a mutation test asserting exactly one recalc is enqueued per change, and
      that two concurrent mutations for the same portfolio cannot interleave into a torn
      series.
- [x] Commit.

Shipped as wallets `v1.1.106` (`1134ff8`), pinned in homelab `1e2f0a71d`. tsc clean,
494 tests green.

**The plan's premise was wrong, so "keep exactly one" was not a meaningful operation.**
Measured, the two mechanisms are **layered, not parallel**: `recalc-queue`'s own header
says *"Passes execute through the global backfill runner"* — the debounce feeds the
serializer, and `enqueueBackfill` is what `refreshQuotes` also calls. Two locks solving
two problems, both load-bearing: the grace timer collapses a broker import's thousands
of mutations into one pass, the runner keeps concurrency at 1 (the 2026-09-19 CPU
saturation fix). **Both stay.**

The genuine duplication was one level down: a single position edit ran **two passes**.
The route called `refreshQuotes` (pricing + today's snapshot, awaited, so the 201 could
return a live price), then `notifyTransactionsChanged` armed its 3s timer and ran
`recalcPortfolioHistory` — whose tail is `refreshQuotesUnlocked`. Pass 2 therefore
redid pass 1's work, and in between `DELETE`d every snapshot row and rebuilt: **1,661
rows deleted and rewritten on IBKR to add one position.**

So the queue now runs a new `recalcPortfolioSeries` (`backfill.ts`): the same
`computeSnapshotBatch` upsert, the same pricing tail, the same return-column and
`current_value` sync, minus the DELETE. What force uniquely bought is dropping rows
*outside* the recomputed window — earliest trade deleted, or a wipe-and-reimport — which
keeps its own path (`POST /:id/recompute` with no `mode`, what §63.6's re-import uses).

**The pricing tail was kept deliberately.** `routes/import.ts` fires neither
`refreshQuotes` nor portfolio-open, so an additive pass that skipped pricing would leave
every imported position with a NULL `market_value` — §70's failure, where a full
18,488-row history sat beside 99 unpriced positions.

Tests: the queue suite is retargeted to the new entry point, plus one-mutation→one-pass
and a peak-concurrency-1 assertion with a start→end trace. `backfill.test.ts` gains
**real, unmocked** coverage: the window is re-valued in place and an out-of-window
orphan row **survives** — the discriminating assertion, since force would drop it.

**A cross-suite leak, caught because a test passed alone and failed in the full run.**
Proving the pricing tail works requires a *successful* quote, which populates the
process-wide, symbol-keyed `quoteCache` in `quotes.ts` — and there was no way to reset
it. A later `recalcPortfolioHistory` suite then ran against a warm cache, priced from
it, and wrote a today's-snapshot row its own assertion said must not exist. Added
`__resetQuoteCachesForTests()`, following the existing `__reset*ForTests` convention.
Worth noting the shape: a test that only *succeeds* is as much a hazard as one that
fails.

### 76.4 — One writer per (portfolio, date) in `value_snapshots`

- [x] Three insert sites — `quotes.ts:520` (live, today), `backfill.ts:1021`
      (`_runBackfillCore`, history), `backfill.ts:1071` (`recalcPortfolioHistory`, batch) —
      and three `syncCurrentValueFromSnapshots` sites: `quotes.ts:540`,
      `backfill.ts:1036`, `backfill.ts:1119`. Whichever ran last wins, and two of them
      target the same `(portfolioId, snapshotDate)` row for today. §76.1 removes the
      *trigger* for the live writer on reads but does not remove the writer.
- [x] Decide the ownership rule and write it down: history belongs to the backfill (only
      it can price a past date from bars); today is owned by exactly one path.
      `computeSnapshotBatch` already accepts a window ending today, so the backfill's
      `mode=upsert` can own today and the live writer can be reduced to refreshing
      quotes on positions.
- [x] This is also what single-sources today's FX choice. The residual IBKR divergence
      (§63.2) is ~1.2% on the FX-heavy portfolio — EUR +70,779, USD −39,104, PLN
      −121,130, base PLN — with the snapshot resolving FX at write time and the headline
      at read time, and today's ECB rate not existing until ~16:00 CET. **One writer
      should be tested against that number before the FX residual is chased as its own
      bug**, because a single writer may remove it entirely.
- [x] Tests: a test asserting a single insert path per date; a test that two concurrent
      writers for the same date cannot both succeed; and the existing equivalence test
      (`backfill.test.ts:835`, `snapshotPortfolioValue equals computeSnapshotBatch for
      the same day`) kept green as the arithmetic guard.
- [x] Commit.


**The rule, stated once and now enforced by the code rather than by convention:**

> `computeSnapshotBatch` owns **every** `(portfolioId, snapshotDate)`, today included
> — reached through `_runBackfillCore` (upsert), `recalcPortfolioSeries` (§76.3) and
> `recalcPortfolioHistory` (force). `snapshotPortfolioValue` is reduced to what
> genuinely needs a live quote: pricing positions and reporting what today is worth.
> It **returns** that value instead of persisting it.

Today had to go to the batch, not the live path, for a concrete reason rather than
tidiness: `refreshQuotesUnlocked` **returns early when there are no open positions**,
so a live-owned today would leave a **cash-only portfolio with no today row at all**.
Only the batch covers that case (§62.4).

**§63.2's race fix is now structurally impossible, not merely ordered.** `c195839`
(v1.1.104) fixed a real race — a fire-and-forget live snapshot write racing the
backfill's `syncCurrentValueFromSnapshots`, which grew across a recompute on IBKR and
was invisible on 9 of 10 portfolios. Two writers of today's row were its precondition;
with one writer there is nothing left to order. Its comment is kept and corrected
rather than deleted, because it is what justifies the `quotedCount === 0` guard that
does survive.

**Consequence, stated rather than hidden:** a write no longer moves `current_value` on
the spot — it lands when the debounced pass runs (~3s). The POST still answers with the
freshly priced position, and the card keeps showing the snapshot's own as-of.

**Seven existing tests asserted the two-writer behaviour and were rewritten onto the
new invariant rather than deleted** — including *"does not resolve before today's
snapshot has been written (the §63.2 race)"*, which now asserts the opposite and says
why. The §53.6/§72.17b equivalence guard survives **intact** by asserting on the
returned value: the two valuation paths must still agree to 6dp, which is the whole
reason that test exists.

New: one row per date across the live path *and* a batch pass (the live path must add
nothing), and concurrent passes converging to a coherent series where each row carries
10x **its own date's** close — a torn write surfaces as a value belonging to another
date. Today's row carries the last close because there is no bar for today yet, which
is why the expectation is derived per row rather than pinned to a fixed date set.

### 76.5 — Verify the read path is pure, then close out

      largest portfolio (IBKR, 108 positions) against a non-writing sibling
      (`/summary-metrics`, `/cash`) **on an authenticated session**. Record the numbers
      in this section. This is the evidence §76 was justified by, and it does not exist
      yet.
- [x] Confirm in PROD that navigating a portfolio no longer changes
      `portfolios.current_value`: read the value, navigate, read it again, assert
      unchanged. Then press the new manual control and assert it *does* change.
- [x] Confirm the cron still prices the fleet with the read path gone — the
      `snapshots-sync.ts:51-63` comment describes the exact failure that appears if
      nothing prices: *"the dashboard understated net worth by ~261k PLN on PROD while
      looking entirely plausible."* After the 13:00 UTC run, assert
      `positions.price_source` is `quote` fleet-wide and no portfolio reports
      `unpricedPositions > 0` that previously had prices.
- [x] Commit, then archive §76 and §63.6 together — §63.6's open §63.2 item is the
      writer half of this section and should not be closed twice.


**Read latency** — measured on an authenticated session, IBKR (108 positions), warm
pod, from the browser. `/positions` is now *faster* than the sibling that never wrote,
so it is no longer the slowest thing on the page:

| endpoint | ms |
|---|---|
| `GET /positions` (warm) | **60** |
| `GET /api/portfolios/:id` | 158 |
| `GET /positions` (cold) | 167 |
| `GET /summary-metrics` | 178 |
| `GET /analytics?timeframe=1Y&benchmarks=SPY` | 293 |

**Read purity in PROD**: navigated the portfolio, its Allocation tab and back to
Holdings. `current_value`, the `value_snapshots` count and `max(price_as_of)` were
byte-identical before and after, and `max_price_as_of` (15:20Z) *predates* the
v1.1.105 rollout (15:58Z) — so the read wrote nothing, rather than writing the same
value again.

**Cron still prices the fleet with the read path gone.** Triggered the real
`snapshotsync-postfx` CronJob (additive, same job the 17:20 UTC schedule runs) so the
new single-writer path would actually be exercised — both scheduled runs predate
v1.1.107. `ok=10 failed=0`, and afterwards:

```
open_pos_total=99   open_pos_quote=99   open_pos_null_mv=0
portfolios_with_today_snapshot=10 / 10   backfill_failed=0
```

`open_pos_null_mv=0` is the §70 requirement specifically: a full history sitting beside
unpriced positions is what understated net worth by ~261k PLN while looking plausible.

**§76.5's last check found a real bug, which is the reason it existed.** The plan says
"press the new manual control and assert it *does* change". It did not change —
`max(price_as_of)`, `current_value` and the snapshot count were all identical after a
successful POST. Cause: §76.2 had pointed the client at `?mode=upsert`, which routed to
`runBackfillRecent` — a pass that re-values the series from prices *already stored* on
the positions and never calls instruments. The force mode it replaced ended in
`refreshQuotesUnlocked`, so moving the control to upsert had silently removed the only
thing that made it do anything. Shipped `v1.1.108`: the additive mode now runs
`recalcPortfolioSeries` (the §76.3 pass, upsert *with* the pricing tail), inside
`enqueueBackfill` since it takes the abort signal and does not enqueue itself. So
"refresh now" does what `snapshots-sync` does for the fleet — price, then re-value.

Re-verified in PROD on v1.1.108:

```
before  max_price_as_of=2026-09-30 16:46:00.782+00   snapshots=1661
after   max_price_as_of=2026-09-30 19:40:01.967+00   snapshots=1661   status=complete
```

The as-of **advanced**, so the control now genuinely re-prices, and the snapshot count
is unchanged — upsert, nothing deleted.

**`current_value` did not move, and that is the correct outcome, not a failed
assertion.** The market was closed and today's ECB rate was already in, so the
recomputed figure is the same number to the eighth decimal. The honest property is
*"pressing it writes and advances the as-of"*, not *"the number changes"* — a value
that only moves when the market moves is the point of §76. §76.5's wording was wrong
about what to assert, and the run that surfaced it is also what proved the check was
worth having.

**One self-inflicted false alarm, retracted.** Mid-check, `kubectl get cronjob | head -10`
appeared to show the `snapshotsync-postfx` CronJob missing — which would have meant the
"twice daily" cadence §76 was built on was actually once daily. It was an artifact of
truncating the list. Both cronjobs exist (`0 13 * * *` and `20 17 * * *`), both ran
today and completed (2m40s and 2m26s). No finding.

## 77. The session is the id_token, so it dies after 60 minutes (found 2026-09-30)

User report: "when logged in, session is too short."

**Diagnosis (verified against prod, not inferred).** The bearer token the SPA
stores is Pocket-ID's **id_token**, and nothing refreshes it.
`portfoliost-users-auth/src/routes/auth.ts:116` returns
`access_token: tokenResponse.id_token`. Decoding the live token out of
`localStorage["portfoliost_token"]` in the browser:

    iss https://pocket-id.k.homylab.com
    aud badb965e4e0be8e26f765f192418cc0c6b2f373f272f9d4886230d3203436e61  (PortfolioST)
    iat 2026-09-30T21:03:15Z   exp 2026-09-30T22:03:15Z   -> lifetime 60 min

Pocket-ID issues the id_token with the client's **access token** duration, so
the session length is exactly `accessTokenDurationMinutes` on the
`PocketIDOIDCClient` CR — live value **60**
(`cluster/apps/networking/pocket-id-operator/app/portfoliost-oidc-client.yaml`).
The same CR has `refreshTokenDurationMinutes: 43200` (30 d): Pocket-ID *does*
issue a 30-day refresh token, `routes/auth.ts` throws it away, and the frontend
never asks. `grep -rn "refresh_token\|grant_type" src/` in `portfoliost` →
zero hits.

**Two things that make this worse than "60 min".**

1. No proactive expiry check. `isAuthenticated` is `Boolean(token)`
   (`src/stores/auth.ts:13`), so an expired token still satisfies the guard at
   `src/router/index.ts:265`. Confirmed live: an expired token yields
   `401 {"error":"Unauthorized","message":"Invalid or expired token"}`, so you
   are ejected mid-task rather than at a login screen.
2. `prompt: "login"` is hardcoded at `src/auth/pkce.ts:65`, so every recovery
   costs a full passkey ceremony.

**Why not just raise `accessTokenDurationMinutes`.** It works — it is the field
I measured the session from — but it buys the session with a long-lived,
non-revocable credential, and it leaves the 30-day refresh token unused. The
refresh grant already rotates the token with a fresh 30-day expiry
(`createTokenFromRefreshToken` → `createRefreshToken`, `ExpiresAt: now + 30d`),
which gives an indefinitely sliding session *and* keeps access tokens short.

**Safety check that made this acceptable.** The refresh path had a known
advisory — GHSA-w6p7-2fxx-4f44, refresh bypassed the disabled-user,
authorization-revocation and group-restriction checks, so a disabled account
kept refreshing forever. Fix commit `978ac87`;
`compare/978ac87...v2.14.0` → `ahead_by: 280, behind_by: 0`, so the deployed
v2.14.0 **contains** it. Long sessions therefore remain revocable by disabling
the user or changing `portfoliost_admin` membership — the next refresh fails.

**This was a conscious deferral, not an oversight.**
`docs/proposals/auth-oidc-pkce-pocketid.md` says so in as many words: *"Token
refresh: Not implemented initially. If the JWT expires, the user must
re-authenticate via PocketID. Can be added later with a refresh token flow."*
§77 closes that. The same proposal's *Risks* section also claims *"The frontend
doesn't check expiry — it relies on 401 responses from the backend. This is
fine."* That is the sentence that hid the mid-task ejection until now.

**`offline_access` is a non-issue — verified, not assumed.** PocketID advertises
`offline_access` in `scopes_supported` and `src/auth/pkce.ts:61` does not
request it, which looked like it would mean no refresh token is ever issued.
Reading PocketID's own sqlite (`pocket-id.db` on the `pocket-id-data` PVC,
copied read-only) settles it:

    oauth2_sessions, kind='refresh_token', client=PortfolioST: 223 rows, all active
      newest: expires_in = 30.0d      (RefreshTokenLifespan = 30 * 24h, provider.go:39)
      oldest: expires_in = -0.6d, still active=1   (never used; no cleanup)

223 unused 30-day refresh tokens — one per login since this shipped, every one
discarded by `routes/auth.ts`. They are issued **without** `offline_access`, so
no scope change is needed. Incidentally this also confirms the sliding window,
and shows expired rows are never cleaned up (a slow leak, harmless).

**Logout does not log out — three separate gaps**, all invisible today because
the session is only 60 min:

1. `POST /api/auth/logout` (`routes/auth.ts:188-190`) is literally
   `return c.json({ success: true })` — no end_session, no revocation.
2. PocketID's session cookie is never cleared, so the OIDC session survives.
   Only the hardcoded `prompt=login` hides it.
3. The OIDC client advertises `logoutCallbackUrls:
   https://portfoliost.${SECRET_DOMAIN}/logout`, but **no `/logout` route
   exists** — `grep -c logout src/router/index.ts` → `0`. Verified in prod:
   visiting `/logout` redirects to `/en/investments`, still authenticated.
   Harmless only because end_session is never called; it must be fixed *before*
   it is, or signing out bounces the browser back into the app.

**Design decisions (resolved).**

- Refresh token lives **server-side** in `users_auth`, SHA-256 hashed, keyed by
  the current id_token's `jti`. It never reaches the browser. `POST
  /api/auth/refresh` takes the (possibly expired) id_token, verifies signature
  **ignoring `exp`**, looks up the row, exchanges, returns a fresh id_token.
  The bearer-token architecture is untouched, so `portfoliost-wallets`,
  `-instruments` and `-admin` need no changes.
- **`logout()` must delete the refresh row in the same change**, and must be
  extended to end the PocketID session and receive its callback. With a 30-day
  refresh token, a logout that only forgets the local token is not a logout.
- **No proactive refresh timer. Refresh-on-401 only.** A timer is a scheduler
  whose only job is to avoid a code path — that is backwards. It would need
  re-arming, cleanup, `exp` parsing, and would be at the mercy of background-tab
  throttling, all to avoid one extra round-trip. "Keeping the risky code rare"
  does not justify it either: close the laptop overnight and the token has
  expired, so the 401 path runs on the first request tomorrow regardless. The
  401 path is event-driven; the timer is scheduled. Cheaper and simpler.
- **A single in-flight refresh is mandatory** — this is correctness, not
  complexity. Measured on prod: one dashboard load fires **15 parallel API
  calls**, 10 of them per-portfolio `analytics`. If all 15 lapse at once and
  each calls refresh independently, rotation invalidates the token after the
  first, so 14 requests fail and the session looks broken. One shared in-flight
  promise, awaited by every concurrent 401, is the minimum that makes this safe.
- Keep `prompt=login`. With refresh working, manual logins are rare, so the
  annoyance mostly disappears, and always showing the passkey is the
  conservative default. Not part of this section.
- No client secret is needed: `isPublic: true` + PKCE, and the helmrelease sets
  only `POCKETID_CLIENT_ID`. users-auth already reaches the token endpoint at
  `http://pocket-id.networking.svc.cluster.local:1411/api/oidc/token`.

**Out of scope: nginx edge auth.** ingress-nginx has no native JWT validation,
and PocketID cannot be an `auth-url` target — tested, `/api/oidc/userinfo`
returns `401` for our token because it wants an *access* token and we ship the
`id_token*; `introspect` needs `client_secret_basic` and the client is public;
`authorize` is a redirect flow. The only viable path is the dormant
`GET /internal/verify` on users-auth (`src/index.ts:34`, never wired). Even then
it would not replace app-side validation — the SPA sends the same
`Authorization` header — so it is defence-in-depth on top, adds a hop per
request, and needs `/login` + `/auth/callback` exempted or it locks you out.
It does not lengthen the session. Belongs in its own section, later.

Scope spans three repos (`portfoliost`, `portfoliost-users-auth`,
`portfoliost-contracts`); the contracts change is the mandatory schema for the
new endpoint, per `AGENTS.md` API-client typing rules.

      `{ id_token: string }`, response `AuthResponse` (already
      `required: [access_token, token_type, user]`, `expires_in: integer`).
      Reusing `AuthResponse` keeps `AuthCallback.vue` and `LoginView.vue`
      unchanged.
- [x] Document in the endpoint description that the supplied `id_token` may be
      expired — expiry is deliberately not checked, signature is.
- [x] `npm run gen:types` in `../portfoliost-contracts/contracts/`, then copy to
      `portfoliost-users-auth/src/generated/api-types.d.ts` and
      `portfoliost/src/generated/api-types.d.ts` (both repos keep their own

- [x] Tests: `npm test` and `npm run lint` green in
      `../portfoliost-contracts/contracts/`.

### 77.2 — users-auth: persist the refresh token at login

- [x] New drizzle table `refreshSessions` in `src/db/schema.ts` under the
      existing `usersAuthSchema` (`users_auth`): `idTokenJti` (text, PK),
      `userId`, `refreshToken` (text), `createdAt`, `updatedAt` (text).
      Model on `userPreferences` — all timestamps are `text` ISO strings in
      this schema, not `timestamptz`.

      **Correction (implemented):** the column is `refreshToken`, stored in the
      clear, not a hash. The refresh grant must replay the value verbatim to
      Pocket-ID, and a hash cannot be exchanged — the first cut stored
      `sha256` and made the session unusable. Accepted on the grounds that
      anyone able to read this database can already read the portfolios and
      positions directly, so the token adds impersonation, not data exposure
      beyond what such a reader already has. No `expiresAt`: the row's lifetime
      is Pocket-ID's 30 days, and the server is the only thing that needs to
      know about it.
- [x] `npm run db:generate` → new file under `drizzle/` alongside
      `0000_baseline.sql`. Inspect the generated SQL: it must create in
      `users_auth`, not the `drizzle_users_auth` migrations schema.
- [x] In `routes/auth.ts`, add the field to the
      `PocketIDTokenResponse` interface (line 18-23) — `refresh_token` is
      currently not even declared.
- [x] After a successful exchange in `POST /api/auth/token`, upsert the row
      keyed by `idPayload.jti`. Return the id_token exactly as today, so the
      existing browser payload is unchanged.
- [x] Tests: extend `src/routes/auth.test.ts`. Stub `fetch` to return a token
      response containing `refresh_token` and `id_token` with a `jti`, then
      assert a `users_auth.refresh_sessions` row exists and that the HTTP
      response body still contains no `refresh_token` key — what must not leak
      is the response, not the row.
- [x] Commit.

### 77.3 — users-auth: the refresh endpoint

- [x] Add `refreshWithPocketID(refreshToken)` in `routes/auth.ts`, mirroring
      `exchangeWithPocketID`: `grant_type=refresh_token`, plus `client_id` and
      the same env vars (`POCKETID_TOKEN_URL`, `POCKETID_CLIENT_ID`). No
      `client_secret`.
- [x] `POST /api/auth/refresh`: read `id_token` from the body → verify with
      `jose.jwtVerify` against the Pocket-ID JWKS using
      `clockTolerance: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (or `jose` option
      `ignoreExpiration`-equivalent) so an expired-but-valid token is accepted.
      Read `sub`, `email`, `groups`, `jti` from the verified payload — from the
      signature, never from the raw request body.
- [x] Look up the row by `jti`. On miss → `401` and delete nothing. On hit →
      exchange, then update the row: new `jti` **as** the key (delete old,
      insert new), new hash, new `expiresAt`. Rotation is required — Pocket-ID
      deletes the consumed refresh token server-side, so reusing the old `jti`
      must fail on the second call.
- [x] Return the same `AuthResponse` shape as `/token`, built from the *new*
      id_token's claims so `groups` stays current.
- [x] Tests in `src/routes/auth.test.ts`, all with a stubbed `fetch` and a
      locally generated RSA keypair served from a stubbed JWKS:
      - expired-but-signed token + valid row → `200`, new `access_token`,
        row re-keyed to the new `jti`;
      - same token replayed a second time → `401` (rotation enforced);
      - valid token with no row → `401`;
      - tampered signature → `401`, and the row is **not** consumed;
      - response contains no `refresh_token` key.
- [x] Commit.

### 77.4 — logout actually revokes (all three parts)

Gap 2 and gap 3 from the intro. This step is not optional: it is what stops
"log out" from becoming a lie once the refresh row exists.

- [x] `POST /api/auth/logout` (`routes/auth.ts:188`) currently returns

      `refresh_sessions` row by `jti`. A missing row is still a `200` —
      logout is idempotent.
- [x] Land that half in `portfoliost-users-auth` first, keeping the body

      tokens are *not* deleted on end-session, so confirm against v2.14.0

- [x] `src/router/index.ts`: add the missing `/logout` route (public, no auth).

- [x] `src/layout/SidebarNav.vue:15` and `src/modules/settings/ProfileView.vue:125`:

### 77.5 — portfoliost frontend: refresh-on-401 with a single in-flight guard

No timer (see intro). One event-driven path.

- [x] `src/api/auth.ts`: add `refresh(idToken)` calling `POST
      /api/auth/refresh`, typed from the regenerated `api-types.d.ts`.
- [x] `src/stores/auth.ts`: add `refreshSession()` that calls it, updates
      `token`/`user`, and `setToken()`. Module-level `let inflight: Promise<void>
      | null` — if set, return it; otherwise create it and clear it in a
      `finally`. Every concurrent 401 awaits the same promise. **This is the part
      that breaks without it**: 15 parallel requests lapse together, the first
      refresh rotates the token, the other 14 find no row and fail.
- [x] `src/api/client.ts` `request()`: on `ApiError` with `status === 401`,
      await the single in-flight refresh, then replay the original request
      **once**. Guard with a per-request `retried` flag so the refresh call
      itself cannot recurse; a failed refresh falls through to `logout()` +
      redirect to `login`.
- [x] State the idempotency reasoning in a comment rather than leaving it
      implicit: replay is safe because the 401 comes from `validateJwt` in
      middleware *before* any handler runs, so no side effect occurred on the
      first attempt. Add a test that a 401'd `POST` replays exactly once and
      the backend sees two requests but one committed effect.
- [x] Leave `prompt: "login"` at `src/auth/pkce.ts:65` alone (resolved above).
- [x] Tests in `src/api/client.spec.ts`:
      - 401 → one refresh → replayed request returns `200`;

      in localStorage, which also breaks the signature, so the app correctly
      treated the session as dead and the test proved nothing about refresh.
      A genuinely expired token is one Pocket-ID signed with a past `exp`; that
      needs either a 60-minute wait or temporarily lowering
      `accessTokenDurationMinutes`. The expired-but-valid-signature path is
      covered by the §77.3 unit tests, not by prod.

- [ ] Prune `refresh_sessions`. It has no cleanup, and the failed expiry

      be verified, so logout cannot identify it and the row survives. Harmless —
      the token is dead — but the table grows without bound. Logout and
      rotation both delete correctly; only unverifiable tokens leak, so a
      periodic sweep (or deleting on `clear-data`/`account`, which already have
      the `user_id` index) would close it.

- [x] `accessTokenDurationMinutes` left at 60, as intended. The fallback (bump to
      `720`) was not needed.
- [x] Closed out and archived here.

## Carried forward from §77

Both are small and neither is urgent. They are recorded rather than forgotten:

1. **Real token expiry was never proven in prod.** Every prod check used a
   genuinely valid token. Simulating expiry locally breaks the signature, which
   makes the app correctly treat the session as dead — so the test proves
   something else. Confirm by letting a session lapse (60 min), or temporarily
   lowering `accessTokenDurationMinutes` and watching one `/api/auth/refresh`
   fire, not fifteen.
2. **Prune `refresh_sessions`.** No cleanup, and the failed expiry simulation
   left one real orphan row: its token cannot be verified, so logout cannot
   identify it and the row survives. Harmless — the token is dead — but the
   table grows unbounded. The `user_id` index already exists for a sweep, and
   `clear-data` / `account` are natural places to delete alongside
   `user_preferences`.

## 72.39 — the recovered openst class-provider plan, in one place (archived 2026-10-01)

> **Archived 2026-10-01 from `plan.md`, with two exceptions kept live.**
> Steps 1, 1b, 2, 3 and the audit are complete and shipped. What remains open is
> carried in §72.40, because a section in this archive must not hold pending
> work: the PROD reimport is unverified, and two sheet-data findings were never
> started. Both are one-liners pointing here, not restatements of the reasoning.

Scattered across §72.6 / §72.16 / §72.19 / §72.20 / §72.23 and contradicted by my own
notes for three turns. Consolidated, with the order that actually matters.

**The problem, stated correctly for the first time.** The broker executes ING Akcji
orders against a price series that is **not** the one `INGAKC.TFI` carries, and the two
diverge over time:

```
date         paid     bar     ratio
2023-08-09   432.49   396.80  1.0899
2024-06-13   515.13   466.96  1.1032
2025-05-13   643.28   575.59  1.1176
2026-08-19   896.00   795.02  1.1270
```

Confirmed by the user: **382,05 is the real executed price** (broker detail, register
total agrees), and there were **no splits** in this fund — matching
`split_adjustments` at 0 rows. The bars already track the provider's live quote
(795.02 vs 820.03 current), so bar and quote are one series and the broker's executions
are priced off another. Growing divergence is the expected signature of two classes
with different fee loads.

**Step 1 — the one check that settles it, and it is two lookups.** ING01's *published*
NAV for the two dates where both numbers are known:

- **2026-08-19** — bar 795.02, paid 896.00
- **2023-04-13** — bar 351.93, paid 382.05

→ ING01 ≈ 896/382 means the bar is the wrong class and the provider is needed.
→ ING01 ≈ 795/352 means orders execute against a class with **no series at all**, which
is a bigger and more interesting finding. Either way the answer changes what gets built,
which is why nothing should be built before it.

**Step 2 — build it, in the planner contract's provider-tier order**, for whichever class
step 1 identifies: fixture into `tests/fixtures/` → openbb plugin with mocked I/O →
openst standalone smoke → `cachest` route → `portfoliost-instruments` adapter → full
compose stack.

**Step 3 — stop the same defect recurring silently.** `ticker_reference` knows **zero**
`.TFI` symbols, so nothing cross-checks a TFI price series against the fund that
actually trades. Add the class once known, and sweep the other `.TFI` rows (the same

            >
            > ### The recogniser is membership-gated, and the plan's assumption was wrong
            >
            > The stage above assumed dotlessness was a usable discriminator. **It is
            > not**, and three measurements against PROD killed every shape-based
            > option:
            >
            > | attempt | result |
            > |---|---|
            > | `fund + letter` transform | impossible — of ING01's nine categories only `ING01/U/W/T/F` resolve; `A/I/K/S/E` are 404 |
            > | "dotless ⇒ category" | **all 941 `corp_bond` rows are dotless** (`ABE0227` = 3 letters + 4 digits) |
            > | digit-count window | `ticker_reference` holds **35,894 symbols with 0–8 digits** (`A`, `ZTM25`, `ZOR1142`, `BE01725053`) |
            >
            > Any regex broad enough to admit `SKR110` also admits a bond. The
            > failure modes are lopsided, which settles the design: **wrongly
            > admitting** a code reroutes a working bond, while **wrongly omitting**
            > one falls through to the equity walk and returns `200 / bars=0` —
            > the silent shape that nearly shipped a broken mapping before. So
            > `FUND_CATEGORY_CODES` is an explicit `Set` in `symbol.ts`, and an
            > entry is added only after the source resolves it.
            >
            > **Two pre-existing findings, recorded because they change the shape of
            > the code:**

            >    special case.** So `.TFI` funds resolved to `"stock"` and reached
            >    the right URL *only because the `stock` and `fund` branches were

            >    effectively dead. It is live now, and the two cases are no longer
            >    interchangeable. Any future divergence in those branches would
            >    have silently changed every fund's price source.
            > 2. **`.TFI` funds are explicitly NOT diverted.** `NNEP65` reproduces
            >    34 of 66 trades to the cent through the existing route, and
            >    `NNEP30`'s first trade sits 17 days inside `ING82`'s window, so
            >    diverting it could silently lose a bar. Pinned by a test.

            > §74.6 were both reaching for and neither could achieve. It also

- [x] Step 3 — sweep the other `.TFI` rows. **Run against PROD 2026-09-30, and
      exactly one symbol was wrong — the one already fixed.**
      > **The sweep was worth more than the fix, because it produced a
      > discriminator that separates the two defects this family confuses.**
      >
      > Method: for each stored BUY/SELL, ask *our own provider* for the bar on that
      > trade's own date and compare to the executed price. No category table, no
      > scraping, no drift assumption — the executed price is the test. 174 trades
      > over 6 symbols, from `portfolios.transactions` via the CNPG pod:
      >
      > | symbol | trades | cent-exact | mean(paid/bar) | trend/yr | verdict |
      > |---|---|---|---|---|---|
      > | `INGAKC.TFI` | 78 | **0** | **1.0840** | **+1.80%** | **wrong class** |
      > | `INGOBL.TFI` | 2 | 0 | 1.0139 | +0.99% | *n too small to judge* |
      > | `NNEP25.TFI` | 2 | 2 | 1.0000 | 0.00% | symbol OK |
      > | `NNEP30.TFI` | 5 | 5 | 1.0000 | 0.00% | symbol OK |
      > | `NNEP60.TFI` | 20 | 2 | 0.9993 | +0.59% | symbol OK |
      > | `NNEP65.TFI` | 66 | **34** | **1.0000** | +0.05% | symbol OK |
      >
      > **The discriminator is trend, not magnitude.** A wrong *unit class* is a
      > systematic offset that **grows** — two classes with different ongoing fees
      > diverge progressively, which §72.38 already worked out. An *order priced at
      > the valuation date* is noise centred on 1.0 with no trend, and its exact hits
      > are precisely the days where the order date and valuation date coincided.
      >
      > **`NNEP65.TFI` is the proof that this works, and it is worth keeping:**
      > 34 of 66 trades match to the cent. A wrong class cannot produce cent-exact
      > identity on half its trades. That is what makes the sweep's negative results
      > credible — "no exact matches" alone would prove nothing, because an
      > order-priced fund produces exactly that on a valuation-date mismatch.
      >
      > So the `.TFI` family is **one wrong symbol, not a class of them**, and it is
      > `INGAKC.TFI` — fixed in sheets-sync `a29dbe3`. The `NNEP*` Emerytura funds
      > and `INGOBL` were always mapped correctly.
      >
      > **`INGOBL.TFI` is flagged, not cleared.** Two trades, and a mean of 1.0139
      > with a +0.99%/yr slope is *shaped* like a small class difference. That is
      > nowhere near enough to act on, and it is recorded rather than quietly
      > dropped into "OK" because the row would otherwise read as verified. It needs
      > either more trades or a deliberate check of whether an alternative category
      > exists — which is the same question step 1b just answered for ING Akcji, and
      > the same method answers it: compare the stored prices against that
      > candidate's series.
      >
      > **What this does not settle.** A symbol can be right and a *class* still
      > wrong in principle; here the 34 cent-exact matches make that moot for
      > `NNEP65`, but the sweep's guarantee is only as good as "the provider serves
      > one class per `.TFI` ticker" — which is an assumption about the provider, not
      > something this measured.

> ## 78. Funds are served but not discoverable — no search path exists for them (2026-10-01)
>
> Raised after §72.39 stages 1–6 were done and proven. The provider work is
> complete: `ING01W` is served, cached and routed, and the three gate readings
> reproduce through the whole tier. **None of that makes a fund findable.** The
> search path was never in scope and is entirely absent.
>
> **The gap, measured rather than assumed:**
>
> | layer | what exists | funds? |
> |---|---|---|
> | openst | `/equity/search`, `/crypto/search`, `/fixedincome/search` | **no fund route** |
> | cachest | proxies all three | **no fund route** |
> | instruments | `searchTickerReference` → `ticker_reference` | **0 fund rows** (PROD) |
> | SPA | `InstrumentSearchModal` → `/api/instruments/search` | returns nothing for any fund |
>
> ### 78.1 — Two precedents exist, and funds need both halves of one dataset
>
> The trap is assuming bonds are searchable the way stocks are. They are not, and
> the two mechanisms are different:
>
> - **Corp bonds** are rows in `ticker_reference` (`WSE::{SYMBOL}`, 941 of them),
>   written by `corp-bond-catalogue-sync.ts` from cachest `/corp-bond/catalogue`.
>   They are searchable *because they are table rows*.
> - **Savings bonds (ROD/EDO) are not in `ticker_reference` at all** — PROD returns
>   0 rows with `asset_type='bond'`. They are searchable because
>   `src/routes/instruments.ts:293` merges an **additive `bondSearchLeg`** that
>   calls openst `/fixedincome/search`.
>
> So there are two routes to searchability: a table row, or a provider leg. Funds
> should get **one dataset that yields both** — because the same rows also settle
> the routing question §72.39 stage 5 had to answer with a hardcoded `Set`.
>
> **Which is why this section also deletes `FUND_CATEGORY_CODES`.** Stage 5's
> membership-gated list exists only because `upstreamFor()` is pure and cannot ask
> the database what a symbol's venue is. If the catalogue lands in
> `ticker_reference`, the tier is readable from those rows' `exchange` column and
> the `Set` — provider knowledge sitting in a service module — becomes deletable.
> Decision taken: **delete it, derive the tier from data.**
>
> ### 78.2 — The catalogue source is the hard part, and it is not a listing page
>
> The bond catalogue scrapes one server-rendered listing. **analizy.pl has no
> equivalent**, verified 2026-10-01:
>
> - `fundusze-inwestycyjne-otwarte/notowania` renders **11** fund links; the page
>   claims ~400 funds.
> - `?strona=`, `?page=`, `?p=` are **all ignored** — 11 links for every value.
> - The table is JS-rendered. The only fund endpoints in `fundCatalogAsync.js` are
>   `/api/fund-observed/` and `/api/fund-in-wallet/` — the observation UI, not a
>   catalogue.
> - Site search (`/wyszukiwarka`, `/szukaj`) is **404**.
>
> So a catalogue scrape is not available and this is **not** a "find the right
> listing page" problem.
>
> **What does work is enumeration by code sweep**, because the codes are cheap to
> probe — one JSON GET each, no auth, and a miss is a clean `404`. Proven twice:
> `ING01`–`ING99` returned every ING category (that sweep is how `ING81`/`82`/`88`
> were found), and a 20-prefix × 2-probe discovery pass resolved
> `ING01 PZU01 PZU50 AXA01 ARK01 ARK50 PCS50 QRS01 SKR01 VIG01`.
>
> **The sweep is bounded and that is a stated limit, not a hidden one:** the prefix
> list is *data* in the repo, and each prefix is probed `01`–`99`. It is blind to
> managers outside the listed prefixes, and it is a refresh job, not a per-request
> call. Sweeping every plausible 3-letter prefix × 99 would be ~100k requests and
> is not proposed.
>
> ### 78.3 — Steps, in the planner contract's provider-tier order
>
> - [x] **Step 1 — catalogue capture.** Manual sweep, one request per code, raw
>       > **DONE** — `openst 3793e68`. **734 categories** across the 8 resolved TFI
>       > prefixes: 259 funds and **475 lettered unit categories**, CSV in the
>       > `/corp-bond/catalogue` shape. Gate PASS — the 7 codes §72.39 verified are
>       > all present with label, currency and first/last valuation; all 734 are PLN
>       > and run to 2026-09-29.
>       >
>       > **It took two passes, and the first failed the gate** — the finding worth
>       > keeping. A numeric sweep of `<prefix><01..120>` returned 259 funds and
>       > **missed `ING01W`**, because a category is the fund code *plus a letter*.
>       > Numeric-only would have dropped 65% of the corpus and, worse, looked
>       > complete: `ING01W` is the symbol the whole class-W build exists for, so its
>       > absence would not have been obvious.
>       >
>       > The second pass probes `<code><letter>` for eleven letters — §72.20's nine
>       > ING01 categories plus `P` (`ING04P`) and `B` (`VIG04B`). That bound is
>       > recorded as a **limit of the catalogue, not a completeness claim**: a
>       > category on a letter outside the set is absent. It is data in the sweep, so
>       > the set widens without a code change. All 26 letters would be ~6.7k
>       > requests.
>       >
>       > Per-fund detail pages were rejected for a concrete reason: they *do* list
>       > all sibling categories in one request, but the slug is mandatory (404
>       > without it) and not derivable — `VIG04B`'s label is "VIG / C-QUADRAT Akcji
>       > B" while its slug is `vig-c-quadrat-akcji`.
>       >
>       > Prefixes were **discovered, not guessed**: 60 candidates probed, exactly 8
>       > resolve. `MAX_NUM` is 120 because `SKR110` is real. Sweeps paced at
>       > 0.25–0.3s, matching the corp-bond job's own spacing.
> - [x] **Step 2 — openst routes.** `GET /fund/catalogue` (CSV) and
>       `GET /fund/search/{query}`, both over the captured catalogue.
>       > **DONE** — `3747f0c`, **31 new tests**, full compose suite green
>       > **447 + 104 + 53 + 21**.
>       >
>       > **The catalogue is a snapshot, not a scrape, and that is the one way this
>       > route differs from `/corp-bond/catalogue`.** That one reads a single
>       > server-rendered page; this corpus is 734 codes across two enumeration
>       > passes (~960 requests), so a request-path scrape is impossible. A refresh
>       > job rewrites `data/fund-catalogue.csv` and the route serves the file.
>       >
>       > **A missing or empty snapshot is a 503, never an empty CSV.** An empty
>       > catalogue would make every fund unsearchable and every fund code a 404 —
>       > indistinguishable from "this source has no funds", the silent shape this
>       > work exists to avoid. A search **miss** is likewise 404, never an empty
>       > 200. Both asserted.
>       >
>       > Search matches code, alias **or** name, substring and case-insensitive,
>       > so the class-W symbol is reachable without knowing its code: `ING01`
>       > returns `ING01W` alongside its siblings, and `akcji` finds it by name. The
>       > tickerref CSV carries the bare fund code in `aliases` for the same reason.
>       >
>       > Two details pinned by tests because they are easy to get wrong:
>       > `_base_fund_code` strips **exactly one** trailing letter (`SKR117B` is a

>
> ### 78.4 — The quote path did not exist, and deploying it surfaced 13 days of release damage
>
> Added after §78's steps shipped. Two things happened that the section above did
> not anticipate, and both are worth more than the code.
>
> **The quote path was missing, not just the search path.** §78 made funds
> *discoverable*; it never made them *priceable*. The distinction cost real work:
> `price-bars.ts` resolves history, but a position is priced from a **quote**
> (`refreshQuotes` → `fetchQuoteByAssetClass` → `current_price`), which had no
> `fund_category` branch at all. A fund position therefore resolved no quote and
> stayed `market_value IS NULL` — excluded from portfolio totals — while §72.39's
> history work looked finished. This was found only because the user's question
> ("will the *recompute* refresh it?") did not match my claim that a recompute would
> fix it; recompute re-derives from *stored* prices and can never fetch one.
>
> So `fetchQuoteByAssetClass` got a `fund_category` branch that maps
> `ticker_reference` row → provider code (`ING01W`, the stored category, **not**
> `GMSAKW.TFI`), calls openst `/fund/history`, and returns the **latest** bar as
> the quote. §78's data-driven tier (`priceTierForSymbol`) then settles routing
> from the row rather than the hardcoded `Set`. Verified in the PROD pod: `ING01W`
> 931.03, `ING01` 816.76, `NNEP65.TFI` 19.81 — the ~12.7% class difference, from the
> live process.
>
> **Deploying it exposed pre-existing damage, not new damage.** `wallets` had been
> un-upgradeable since **2026-09-18** — 13 days, three stale references from one
> `app → portfoliost-wallets` rename, each invisible until the previous was cleared:
>
> 1. `controllers.app` (`controller:`/`ports:`) — rejected by app-template@5.1.0's schema;
> 2. `serviceMonitor.app` against an empty `values.service` — *"No enabled Service found with this identifier"*;
> 3. a comma-separated `schedule` — k3s v1.36.2 rejects it: `expected exactly 5 fields, found 10`.
>
> Any wallets deploy in that window would have failed, **including this one**. Same
> shape as §78's cachest config drift: a stale copy of a value nothing reads,
> sitting between the repo and the cluster. Removed the job block, added
> `values.service.app`, and the release went `Ready=True` on revision v150 for the
> first time in 13 days.
>
> **The two snapshotsync CronJobs stayed two.** Consolidating them is correct and
> would make `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid` actually guard both windows (it never did
> — a slow morning pass could still be running when the evening one started, both
> writing prices for one portfolio), but the comma-separated schedule is what this
> cluster rejects. Shipped as **one CronJob at one window** (11:00 UTC). The cost is
> real and is recorded in the manifest: the post-FX pass after the 17:10 CEST
> fxsync settles the ECB rate is gone, so day-end converted values settle the next
> morning. Both jobs were briefly absent entirely — that was only ever to unblock
> the release, and since §76.1 made `snapshots-sync` the **only** writer of
> `positions.market_value`, their absence is a price-staleness risk, not a
> cosmetic detail.
>
> **Verified PROD close-out** (`instruments` v1.0.87, `sheets-sync` v1.0.33,
> `openst` v1.1.43, `cachest` v1.0.48):
>
> | | |
> |---|---|
> | Wipe & Reimport | 80 `ING01W` trades; **51/80 exact to the cent** (was 0/78 vs class A) |
> | 1,845 W bars stored | `ING01W` position `current_price` **931.03**, `price_source` `quote`, value 198,019.07 |
> | names | all six funds show current ING names; 0 stale brands |
> | `actualni kurs` finding (§72.40) | **closed** — user corrected the sheet to 921.19, ratio vs W **1.0000** (was 1.1768), `average_cost_basis` re-derived 459.44 → 458.53, quantity 1.176847 confirmed authoritative |
>
> The gate rail worked as designed: W's nearest bars bracket the disputed 1084.10
> (904.80 / 931.03), so the *cell was provably wrong* — not merely implausible — and
> §74's read-only rule held throughout. Neither we nor any tooling ever wrote to the
> sheet; the correction was the user's.

## 67. Follow-ups from the currency work — the aggregate base and a duplicated helper (2026-09-27)

Two things §66 deliberately did not do, both left over from the rollout.

### 67.1 — the aggregate still denominates in USD, so §63.3 cannot reconcile

`total-metrics` no longer *hardcodes* USD (§66.4) — it uses
`preferredBaseCurrency`, and falls back to the user's own most common portfolio
base when the preference service is unreadable. In PROD that preference is
genuinely **unset**, so the honest default applies and the response still reports
`baseCurrency: "USD"`, while every portfolio is PLN and the cards render PLN.

Measured after the §66 rollout:

| surface | value |
|---|---|
| Σ the 10 cards (Value) | PLN **1,380,487.34** |
| "Total Value" headline | PLN **1,035,259.30** |
| difference | PLN **345,228.04** ≈ the Cash card (PLN 345,228.05) |

So the residual gap is cash, not FX: the cards include cash and the headline
does not. That is §63.3's item, but it is blocked on this: the aggregate needs a
base currency that means something to the user.

- [x] Make the Display-currency selector write through to the user's
      `baseCurrency` preference, so the backend can see it at all
      (`portfoliost` `1d1dd65`, 402 green, **committed but deliberately not
      deployed** — flipping the aggregate base USD → PLN moves the headline, and
      it ships with §68 so the numbers move once, for one reason).
- [x] On deploy (with §68): confirm the aggregate base is now the user's chosen
      currency rather than the USD default.
- [x] Then close §63.3's reconciliation item: headline total == Σ cards, and
      decide whether the headline includes cash (the cards do).
- [x] Also still open there: `Crypto` reports `totalValue: 0,
      returnPercentage: -100` in the breakdown while holding 887.74 PLN and its
      card reads +1.65%. A portfolio with cash and a position must not floor at
      zero.
- [x] Tests: `total-metrics.baseCurrency` is a real base; headline == Σ cards;
      no portfolio in the breakdown reports 0 while holding a position.
- [x] Commit.
      > `1d1dd65` "feat(spa): the Display-currency selector IS the base-currency
      > preference (§67.1)". The commit landed; this box was simply never ticked
      > because the step that followed it (§68) absorbed the closeout.

#### Pre-existing e2e failures found while verifying (not caused by §67.2)

Baseline-checked by stashing the change and re-running: **5 e2e tests already
fail on unmodified `main`** — all of them "chart element not found"
(`chart-recompute.spec.ts:13`, `combined-chart.spec.ts:11` and `:19`,
`performance-display-currency.spec.ts:39`, `parity-portfolios.spec.ts:53`). The
mock backend appears not to serve the charting series these specs wait on.
`portfolios.spec.ts` is separately **flaky** (a different test in it failed on

a release gate for chart work.
