## 81. Drawdowns and annualization both ignore cash flows (2026-10-02)

**Deployed to PROD 2026-10-02** — `portfoliost-wallets` v1.1.118 → **v1.1.119**,
SPA v1.0.350 → **v1.0.352** (skipped v1.0.351, which was docs-only: the §80
archive commit, no `src/` change). Homelab commit `0444edd`. Both wallets pins
moved together — the app Deployment and the `snapshotsync` CronJob run the same
image, and a skew would leave the nightly snapshot job on the code that produced
the wrong columns.

PROD was the right place to measure this: it has real cash flows (398 snapshot
rows carrying 709,710 across 10 portfolios), whereas the compose seed has
`net_flow = 0` everywhere and so cannot tell the flow-neutral path from the raw
one at all.

### PROD verification

Risk-metrics before (wallets v1.1.118) → after (v1.1.119), same portfolios,
same auth:

| portfolio | window | metric | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NN TFI PPK | ALL | `periodReturnPercent` | **28692.61** | **129.52** |
| NN TFI PPK | ALL | `volatility` | 0.356 | 0.124 |
| NN TFI PPK | ALL | `maxDrawdown` | −0.143 | **−0.2806** |
| NN TFI PPK | ALL | `annualizedReturn` | 0.777 | 0.130 |
| NN TFI PPK | ALL | `sortinoRatio` | 7.26 | 0.92 |
| IBKR | ALL | `periodReturnPercent` | **6633.52** | **−1.28** |
| IBKR | ALL | `maxDrawdown` | −0.2954 | −0.4407 |
| IBKR | ALL | `sharpeRatio` | 0.76 | −0.14 |
| Equate+ | 1Y | `periodReturnPercent` | **82.46** | **−18.69** |
| Equate+ | 1Y | `sharpeRatio` | 0.20 | **−0.83** |
| Equate+ | 1Y | `volatility` | 1.809 | 0.266 |

Three things this table settles that the unit tests could not:

1. **A 28,692% period return and a 6,633% one were on screen.** Both were
   deposits booked as profit. §81.1 removes them.
2. **Drawdowns were being truncated, not just over-stated.** NN TFI PPK's real
   drawdown is −28.1%, not −14.3%: the deposits were resetting the running peak
   halfway through. IBKR ALL was −29.5% reported against −44.1% real.
3. **Two portfolios flipped Sharpe's sign.** Equate+ went +0.20 → −0.83 and IBKR
   ALL +0.76 → −0.14. Equate+ is the clearer tell: before the fix, its
   `periodReturnPercent` was **+82.46%** while its `moneyWeightedReturn` was
   **−23.57%** — two independent measures of the same portfolio disagreeing in
   sign, which is exactly what "€ came out, not in" looks like. After the fix
   they agree: −18.69% and −23.57%. The two measures agreeing is the real proof
   the series is now flow-neutral; the individual numbers moving is just
   arithmetic catching up.

§81.2's exponent was verified independently in PROD rather than trusted: for
every portfolio, the years implied by `(1 + periodReturnPercent/100)` and
`annualizedReturn` must equal the elapsed span of the series.

| portfolio | span | implied years | actual years |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NN TFI PPK | 2483 pts, 2482 d | 6.798 | 6.800 |
| Equate+ | 2704 pts, 2703 d | 7.407 | 7.405 |
| IBKR | 1663 pts, 1662 d | 4.594 | 4.553 |

IBKR's residual is not drift: `annualizedReturn` is rounded to 4 dp and its
value is −0.0028, so with a near-zero numerator the implied years is extremely
sensitive. Every 1Y window returns `annualizedReturn` numerically equal to
`periodReturnPercent`, which is the 365/365 case and a further check that the
exponent is 365 and not 252.

UI verified in PROD after the rollout: Equate+'s Drawdown card reads Max −37.00%
/ Current −20.30% — the current drawdown shallower than the maximum, which is the
§81.3 property that the two tiles are finally on one series. Risk tab tiles
render with **zero console errors**.

### What §81.4 deliberately traded away

`volatility`, `sharpeRatio` and `sortinoRatio` now annualise on 365 days, so our
figures are **not comparable** with example-service or with published Sharpe ratios, which
quote √252. User decision 2026-10-02, recorded because it is a choice and not a
correction: on the compose Top10 portfolio this moved volatility 0.1414 → 0.1702
(+20.4% = √(365/252)), Sharpe 2.71 → 3.40, Sortino 3.10 → 3.90.

The benchmark volatility in `backfill.ts` keeps √252 — correctly, because it
reads provider price bars, which are trading days only (verified on
`instruments.price_bars_all`: 0 weekend bars, Mon–Fri ~10.9k rows each). So the
portfolio and its benchmark now use *different* constants, each right for its own
series. If someone later "fixes" that asymmetry by making them match, they will
break the benchmark side.

### Two plan errors found while implementing, both corrected in place

- **§81.2's quarterly example was wrong.** It read "a quarter gives `n ≈ 91`,
  exponent `252/91 = 2.77`, so +5.0% in three months is reported as +14.5%
  annualized", implying +5.0% was correct. It is not: annualising a quarterly
  return to a yearly rate is *supposed* to exceed it. 14.6% was the **old**
  code's output; the corrected exponent gives **+21.9%**. Both are now pinned in
  `riskMetrics.test.ts` so neither can drift again.
- **§81.3's e2e premise was wrong.** It assumed the compose seed carries a
  flow-bearing portfolio. `SELECT count(DISTINCT net_flow)` returns 1 for every
  seeded portfolio and `max(abs(net_flow))` is 0, so `value` and
  `cumulative_twr` are exactly proportional and *no* seeded portfolio can tell
  the two paths apart. The e2e now splices a flow-bearing series into the
  analytics response with `page.route()`, and was verified to fail against the
  old raw-value implementation and pass against the new one.

### The §81.1 invariant is narrower than the plan claimed

"A deposit mid-window returns the same metric as the same series with the
deposit removed" holds **only where no price moves after the flow**. End-of-day
values cannot recover a daily return against a capital base that changed, and the
same €3 on €51,017 genuinely is a smaller return than on €1,017 — the post-deposit
portfolio really is less volatile in percentage terms. The tests now state this
instead of asserting an invariance that does not exist.

### Adjacent defect found, NOT fixed — not planned

`PortfolioRiskTab.vue` passes `volatility` and `maxDrawdown` to `formatPercent`
without scaling, so the Risk tab renders them **100× too small** (`-0.37%` for a
−37% drawdown, `0.27%` for 26.6% volatility). The contract declares both as a
bare `number` with no unit, and the payload mixes units — `volatility` and
`maxDrawdown` are fractions while `winRate` and `periodReturnPercent` are
percents. `PortfolioPerformanceTab.vue` compensates with an explicit `v * 100`
and a comment; the Risk tab does not. Pre-existing, not caused by §81 (the
pre-deploy value 1.809 would have rendered `1.81%`).

## 84. Accounts balance tab — per-account value, deposits and P/L table (D84)

Source: the `Konto` summary block of the source spreadsheet (columns M–S). The
ten `Konto` values are the ten **portfolios** in PROD — verified 2026-10-02:
`IB` is the only renamed account (`IBKR`), the other nine match by name. The row
unit is a portfolio, not a wallet, so no new entity is introduced and no join to
the sheet's own catalog is needed.

Column semantics, as the spreadsheet defines them:

| # | Column | Definition | Payload field |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Account | portfolio name | `name` |
| 2 | Investments | instruments' current value | `instrumentsValue` |
| 3 | Free cash | current free cash, not invested | `cashValue` |
| 4 | Total | 2 + 3 | `totalValue` |
| 5 | Deposits | inflow − outflow **± transfer** to the account | `totalInvested` |
| 6 | P/L | 4 − 5 | derived |
| 7 | Return % | 6 / 5 | `returnPercentage` |

**Every field is already on `PortfolioTotalMetrics.portfolioBreakdown`, so this
section adds no contract field, no backend route and no new endpoint.** Column 6
is the derivation the store already performs at `stores/portfolios.ts:219`; this
tab reuses it rather than writing a second copy.

Two properties of the payload make the table exact rather than approximate, and
both are load-bearing — do not "simplify" either away:

- **Column 4 = column 2 + column 3 holds to the cent.** `portfolios.ts:350-351`
  rounds `instrumentsValue` and `cashValue` *first* and sets `totalValue` from
  the rounded parts (`:367-369`), so the contract's promise is literally kept.
- **Column 5 already includes transfers.** The breakdown reads the denormalized
  `portfolios.totalInvested` column, written by `externalCashInvested`
  (`cashLedger.ts:329`) = Σ DEPOSIT − Σ WITHDRAWAL **± TRANSFER legs**. Verified
  arithmetically on IBKR in PROD: deposits ≈ 15.9k PLN, withdrawals −121 130 PLN,
  net transfers +69 420,89 EUR, summing at an implied ~4,43 PLN/EUR to the
  202 750,68 the endpoint returns. A deposits-only basis could not produce it.

Including transfers in the basis is what makes `Total − Deposits` an identity.
Excluding them would leave the two columns on different conventions — `cashValue`
is a *balance* and must count an own-account transfer that arrived, while a
transfers-free *flow* basis would not — and the P/L of such a row would silently
contain that transfer.

Recorded decisions (resolved with the user):

- **New tab, first in the strip, and the landing page.** `Accounts balance` at
  `/en/investments/accounts-balance`; `/` and the sidebar point at it.
  `/en/investments` keeps working, so no existing deep link or e2e breaks.
- **Exactly these seven columns plus a bold Σ footer.** No share-of-total column
  (`weight` is already on the cards), no per-row unpriced/stale marker.
- **Rows are links** to `/en/portfolios/:id/holdings`.
- **One repo, `portfoliost`.** The provider tier (openst → cachest → instruments)
  does not apply: no new data source, no scraping, no `config.yaml` route.
- **Ordering vs §83:** §83.6 also edits `InvestmentsTabs.vue` and adds a tab after
  `Portfolios`. No conflict — the strip ends up Accounts balance → Portfolios →
  Performance → Transactions → Watchlists — but land whichever lands first and let
  the other edit the same array.

Five exact matches, and the two expected gaps came out at exactly the figures the

Both edge rows behave as designed on live data: **XTB** renders Free cash
`-PLN 24.26` (sign kept) with Return % `—` on `Deposits 0.00`, and **Equate+**
renders `-PLN 6,033.85` / `-25.24%` rather than a clamped zero.

Also verified in the browser: default sort Total desc; every column sortable in
both directions with a `null` Return % last in both; a row click reaching
`/en/portfolios/4242385c…/holdings` (Crypto); the Account cell a real
`<a href>`; the display-currency selector re-denominating the columns; no console
errors. The display currency was left on PLN, as found.

### Σ rows == the headline exactly — but only WITHIN one payload

Checked on the exact response the page rendered from: Σ rows equals the header on
all four money columns (1 058 679,65 / 41 267,29 / 1 099 946,94 / 746 100,99), and
`totalValue == instrumentsValue + cashValue` holds to the cent on all ten rows.

Across **two separate fetches seconds apart** it does not: cash moved
41 267,29 → 41 267,31 and `totalInvested` 746 100,99 → 746 100,97, and one response
mid-session came back with `baseCurrency: DKK` where the next returned PLN. The
aggregate re-converts the multi-currency cash ledger at *latest* rates that tick
between calls. A first PROD pass therefore showed the footer at PLN 1 099 946,94
against a tile at 1 099 946,95 — the payload had moved, not the arithmetic.

This is why the e2e asserts the footer against `tile-total-value` with a
**1-unit tolerance** and not byte equality. A byte-equality assertion would be a
flake waiting for a price tick, and "fixing" it by making the footer read the
headline instead of Σ rows would be worse: the footer would then disagree with
the Total column printed directly above it.

### The table fits at 1280 and scrolls below it

Intrinsic need ≈ 1 008 px. At a 1280 viewport the overflow is 2 px (float hair);
at 1200 it is 82 px and Return % needs the horizontal scroller — the same
behaviour `TransactionsTable` has below its design width. Left as is.

### Adjacent finding, NOT fixed — the fixture rows are not portfolios

The mock's `/api/portfolios` carries Top10 alone, so the seed's other three
breakdown rows are fixture-only: in mock mode their links would 404. Nothing in
the mock or the suite follows them, and e2e reads the real `wallets` service, so
nothing observes it. Adding three portfolios to `portfolios_summaries.json` would
make the mock internally consistent and is the obvious follow-up if anyone ever
runs the SPA against the mock.

## 82. Performance tab: overview tiles & per-year returns (D85–D89)

Proposal: [performance.md](proposals/performance.md) — make the Performance tab
answer "how much more cash than I put in?" and "how efficiently is it invested,
per year and overall".

One new card above the Performance Chart (five tiles) and a `Monthly | Yearly`
toggle on the existing Returns Chart. Touches `portfoliost` and
`portfoliost-wallets` only — **no contract change**, because every field the
proposal needs is already declared in `openapi.yaml` and three of them are
already computed by the route and returned to a UI that displays none of them
(`portfolios.ts:1345-1359`). Risk ratios stay on the Risk tab.

The provider-tier ordering (openst → cachest → instruments) does not apply: no
new data source, no scraping, no route in `config.yaml`. Steps run
backend → SPA tiles → per-year table → benchmark column → parity + full suite.

**Dependency:** TWR p.a. must be annualised over *elapsed calendar years from
the flow-neutral index*. §81.2 is where that number gets built correctly; this
section consumes it and must not re-derive annualization independently.

---

### 82.1 — Populate `performance.annualizedReturn` with the flow-neutral annualised rate

The only backend change in this section. `annualizedReturn` and
`annualizedReturnWithheldReason` are declared in the contract
(`openapi.yaml:1447`, `:1449`) and the analytics route returns **neither** — the
`performance` object it builds ends at `simpleReturnPercent`
(`portfolios.ts:1343-1360`). The SPA therefore has nothing to render a TWR p.a.
tile from.

- [x] **Compute the TWR p.a. in the analytics route** from the already-selected
      `cumulativeTwr` column, annualising over elapsed calendar days:
      `(twr_last / 100) ** (365 / calendarDays(first, last)) − 1`, expressed as a
      **percentage** to match every sibling in `performance.*`
      (`totalReturnPercent`, `moneyWeightedReturn`, `timeWeightedReturn` are all
      percents). Use the existing `daysBetween` helper in
      `src/services/returnColumns.ts` rather than a second date-difference

      = `cumulativeTwr(last of y) / cumulativeTwr(last of y−1) − 1`; year gain
      = `[value − invested](end of y) − [value − invested](start of y)`. The

      > `isYtd` is testable. A year whose last point has no `cumulative_twr` is
      > **skipped**, not shown as 0.00% — 0.00% is a claim about the year and an

### 82.6 — PROD verification, and the `Σ gains` reconciliation D88 got wrong

**Deployed to PROD 2026-10-02** — `portfoliost-wallets` v1.1.119 → **v1.1.120**,
SPA v1.0.354 → **v1.0.356** (v1.0.355 was the docs-only §84 archive commit, no
`src/` change). Homelab commit `af7c4898b`. Both wallets pins moved together —
the app Deployment and the `snapshotsync` CronJob run the same image. Tags read
from `gh release list`, and the checkout was 2 auto-update commits behind, so the
bump was rebased onto the deployed revision. Flux reconciled both kustomizations
at `main@sha1:af7c4898b`; both Deployments rolled out clean, no errors in the
wallets log.

| portfolio | window | metric | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Equate+ | 1Y | `periodReturnPercent` (§81, already in PROD) | **−18.69** | — |
| Equate+ | 1Y | Overview → **TWR p.a.** | tile did not exist | **−18.69%** |
| Equate+ | 1Y | Overview → **XIRR** | tile did not exist | **−23.57%** |
| Equate+ | ALL | Overview → **TWR p.a.** | tile did not exist | **+3.23%** |

The 1Y row is the useful one: §81's archive records that *"every 1Y window
returns `annualizedReturn` numerically equal to `periodReturnPercent`, which is
the 365/365 case and a further check that the exponent is 365 and not 252."* The
new tile reads −18.69% on that same window — an independent confirmation, from
a different code path, that §82.1 is wired to §81.2's number rather than to a
third annualiser. XIRR reads −23.57%, the same `moneyWeightedReturn` §81 verified.
The Timing tile then prints −4.88% / "adding money hurt", which is exactly the
gap between those two figures.

Equate+'s yearly table (ALL): 2019 +7.85% … 2024 +51.00% … 2026 YTD −10.41%,
Σ `× 1.2655`. Verified in SQL against `value_snapshots`:
`cumulative_twr(last)/cumulative_twr(first)` = 126.55/100 = **1.2655** — the TWR
reconciliation holds exactly in PROD, not just in fixtures.

**In compose the Timing tile is unreachable.** The §75 seed writes 49
`value_snapshots` rows, below the 60-point floor the shared withholding predicate
imposes, so Top10 renders `TWR p.a. —` / "not enough history yet" and hides the
Timing line. That is §82.1's decision behaving correctly on thin data; PROD's
portfolios carry 1 663–2 704 points and all four rate tiles are populated.

#### The defect this deploy found: `Σ gains` ≠ `performance.totalReturn`

The two reconciliations are NOT equivalent, and D88 claimed they were. `Σ gains`
telescopes to `net(last) − net(first)`, so it equals `totalReturn` **only for a
series that opens at net 0**. Measured across all ten PROD portfolios:

| portfolio | opening net | `totalReturn` (tile) | `Σ gains` (footer) | gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| IKE Marek | −2 610.72 | 37 314.36 | 39 925.08 | **7.00 %** |
| Crypto | −7.20 | 16.16 | 23.37 | **44.56 %** |
| XTB | −1.90 | −24.08 | −22.18 | 7.89 % |
| IKE Beata | −62.76 | 72 575.14 | 72 637.90 | 0.09 % |
| Equate+ | −19.77 | −6 388.76 | −6 368.99 | 0.31 % |
| IBKR | +2.88 | 76 629.39 | 76 626.52 | 0.00 % |
| NN TFI PPO / PPK, Rach. PKO BP, Obligacje PKO SA Beata | 0.00 | — | equal | 0 % |

Six of ten disagree, and two by enough to matter. The arithmetic is not wrong —
the two numbers measure different windows: the tile reports gain since inception,
the footer reports gain accumulated across the displayed series. The trap is that
they sit on the same card looking like one figure.

**Why nothing caught it.** The compose seed opens at net 0 for every portfolio,
so every fixture and the §82.5 e2e passed. The assertion was true of the test
data and false of the data that exists. Only the deploy surfaced it.

**Two causes, and they are not the same defect.** `unpriced_value` on the first
snapshot explains IKE Marek's 2 605.72 of its 2 610.72 — day-1 positions the
backfill had no price bar for, which the app already reports as
`heldGapSymbols`. Crypto, Equate+, XTB and IKE Beata open with `unpriced_value`
0.00, so theirs are small real opening values (fees, FX, partial pricing), not a
pricing hole. Suppressing the first row's Gain would fix only the first kind and
would misattribute the rest.

**The data fix is already planned and is not §82's.** User decision 2026-10-02:
the opening-net values belong to **§78.1** (XTB's missing `Wpłata` row) and
**§78.2** (IBKR / IKE Marek / IKE Beata's missing ledger rows) — those are the
accounts with a non-zero opening net, and §78.2's own table already shows IKE
Marek running ~4 k *ahead* of what the ledger explains. §82 therefore does **not**
change the derivation or the UI; it stops asserting the false invariant:

- The §82.3 unit test now asserts the true identity
  (`Σ gains = totalReturn − openingNet`) and carries a PROD-shaped fixture built
  from IKE Marek's numbers, which the original assertion fails.
- The §82.5 e2e reads `openingNet` from the payload and subtracts it, and its
  post-switch assertion is now on the shared **rate** (`tile / Σ` equals
  `totalReturn / expectedGain`) rather than on two text strings being equal —
  which is the property the case was always meant to test.
- Re-verified by mutation: dropping the Σ footer's conversion still fails it,
  now with `Expected: 1 / Received: 3.98`.

No UI change, so no re-deploy for this step. When §78 lands and the opening nets
go to zero, the bare equality becomes true on its own and the subtraction becomes
a no-op — which is the right shape for a fix that is about to arrive.

## 83. Cumulative (all-portfolios) Performance tab (2026-10-02)

User request (no proposal file): "a performance tab for cumulative portfolio —
maybe make a component out of the existing per-portfolio tab and just load all
data into it?"

Placed as an **additional tab on the main Portfolios page** (`InvestmentsTabs`),
not a route under `/portfolios/:id`, because it aggregates over all portfolios
and therefore has no `:id`. Built the way the request suggests: extract
`PortfolioPerformanceTab.vue`'s body into a prop-driven component and mount it
twice — per-portfolio from the existing route, and for the account from a new
`/investments/performance` route backed by `GET /api/portfolios/merged`.

**Half of the reuse already exists.** `PortfolioPerformanceChart.vue` is
deliberately one component with no variant prop (§41: *"the charts differ only in
the data delivered"*), and the combined chart on
`src/modules/portfolios/InvestmentsView.vue:382-410`
already uses it. Do not add a second chart or a `combined` prop.

**The other half is the blocker.** "Load all data into it" cannot work as stated,
because the aggregate's return columns do not exist and cannot be read off a sum
of per-portfolio columns. `buildMergedPerformance` (`mergedAnalytics.ts:146-163`)
returns `timeSeries[]` as `{date, value, invested}` only and hard-nulls
`timeWeightedReturn` / `moneyWeightedReturn` with `monthlyReturns: []`; §82.1
does not reach it either, since it scopes to `/:id/analytics`.

The fix is structural, not cosmetic, and it is short: **select `net_flow`
alongside `value` in `/merged` and run the same builders on the summed series.**
`(ΣVₜ) / (ΣVₜ₋₁ + ΣFₜ) − 1` *is* the aggregate's daily return, so no
per-portfolio weighting is needed and no portfolio is privileged.
`buildDailyReturns(values, flows)` (`returnColumns.ts:43`) is already exactly
that expression, and it is now the single implementation §81.1 established — this
section consumes it and must not re-derive it. `netFlow` is external-only per
portfolio (§62.4/D50), so a transfer between two of the user's own portfolios is
excluded on both legs and cancels in the sum.

**Dependency: satisfied.** §81.1–81.3 landed in `811d942`. What this section
builds on, by name:

- `buildDailyReturns(values, flows)` / `chainReturns(returns)` / `buildTwr` —
  `returnColumns.ts:43` / `:53` / `:63`
- `computeRiskMetrics(returns, dates, riskFreeRate?)` — `riskMetrics.ts:242`,
  **pure**, and it returns `maxDrawdown`, `annualizedReturn` and the withheld
  reason. This is why §83.4 needs no new route and no contract change.
- `currentDrawdownPercent(points)` — `src/utils/drawdown.ts`, reads `cumulativeTwr`
  first with a raw-`value` fallback (§81.3)

**Ordering: satisfied.** §81.1–81.3 landed in `811d942`; §82 landed in `05c6855`,
`d02a289`, `a3275be`, `b667c5d`, `ed62b62`. §83.1 now edits the file §82.2–82.4
also edited, so the D85–D89 metrics are already in it — §83.1 is the extraction,
not the introduction.

**Revised 2026-10-02 after §82 landed — what that changed here.** §83 was drafted
against a `PortfolioPerformanceTab.vue` that had no Overview card, one Returns
Chart and no per-year view. It is now 788 lines carrying all of that, so three
things in this section are no longer accurate as written and are corrected in
place below:

1. **The tab grew a second consumer-shaped dependency.** §82.2's Overview card
   (Net gain / Net invested / XIRR / TWR p.a. / Timing) and §82.3's Monthly |
   Yearly toggle read `performance.annualizedReturn`,
   `annualizedReturnWithheldReason`, `moneyWeightedReturn`,
   `moneyWeightedReturnWithheldReason` and `timeframe`. So §83.2 must populate
   `annualizedReturn` **and its withheld reason** on the aggregate, not just the
   return scalars — a tab whose TWR p.a. tile always renders `—` while the
   per-portfolio tab shows a number is the exact "looks like a working page"
   failure §83.6's last test is written to catch. §83.3 and §83.4 are unaffected:
   benchmarks and risk ratios were already declared.
2. **§83.1's extraction surface grew.** Four more things cannot move as-is and
   must become props or internal state: `store.analyticsTimeframe` (which gates
   the Yearly toggle's availability, `:467`), `firstBenchmark` (`:485`),
   `excessByYear` (`:488`), and the `<script lang="ts">` block (`:1-117`) holding
   `yearlyReturns` / `benchmarkYearlyReturns` / `yearlyTotals`. The math block
   travels *with* the template — it is the D88 derivation the Yearly table needs —
   so the existing unit test's import path changes (one line; §83.1).
3. **The FX caveat moved from a footnote to the headline.** §82.2's two money
   tiles (`totalReturn`, `totalInvested`) are the numbers a reader checks against
   their own bank balance, and on a multi-currency aggregate they are the most
   constant-currency-shaped figures on the page. §83.6 says so where those tiles
   are, not only in a footnote under the chart.

Recorded decisions (resolved with the user):

- **Benchmarks need no contract change and no persistence.** `benchmarks[]` is
  already declared on `PortfolioAnalytics` (`openapi.yaml:1545`); `/merged`
  simply ignores the query param today. The selection is per-request store state
  (`stores/portfolios.ts:81-91`), not a DB column, so there is no schema to add.
- **Performers need one contract addition** — see §83.5. `/held-stocks`
  (`portfolios.ts:498`) is *not* reusable: it aggregates by symbol across
  portfolios, drops P/L entirely, and hardcodes `changePercent: 0`.
- **The existing `combined-chart` card is replaced, not duplicated.**
  `InvestmentsView.vue:382-410` renders the same endpoint through the same chart;
  leaving both puts the same curve on two adjacent pages.
- **FX is constant-currency by construction** and the tab must say so — see §83.6.

### 83.2 — `/merged`: sum the flows and build the aggregate return columns

The only step that makes the tab possible. Everything after it is presentation.

- [x] **Add `netFlow`, `unpricedValue` and `carriedValue`** to the `/merged`
      SELECT (`portfolios.ts:786-792`) and thread all three through
      `sumSnapshotsByDateForwardFilled` (`mergedAnalytics.ts:83`) so the aggregate
      sums them per date exactly as it already sums `value` / `invested`. A
      portfolio with no row on date *d* contributes its carried value and **0**
      flow, so its slice of that day's return is 0 — which is correct, not an
      omission.
      > The two withheld amounts are not optional. They are what fires
      > `PortfolioPerformanceChart`'s §78.5 chip (`:109-146`), which reports
      > *"up to 10,465 PLN is missing from this curve"*. Omitting them reuses a
      > chart component with its honesty warning silently disarmed — on the one
      > screen where a wrong total is most expensive. `unpricedValue` must stay
      > **absent rather than 0** on a row that predates the column, for the reason
      > the per-portfolio route spells out at `portfolios.ts:1268-1277`.
- [x] **Chain the aggregate TWR** through `buildDailyReturns` + `chainReturns`
      (`returnColumns.ts:43`, `:53`) — the same path `buildTwr` takes. Do not
      re-derive `Vₜ/(Vₜ₋₁+Fₜ)−1` here, and do not read any stored
      `cumulative_twr` column: those are per-portfolio and summing indices is
      meaningless.
- [x] **Emit per-point `cumulativeTwr`** on the aggregate series, and the scalars
      `timeWeightedReturn` / `moneyWeightedReturn` / `simpleReturnPercent` from
      the last index point, mirroring `:1381-1389`. The aggregate MWR has no
      stored `cumulative_mwr` column to read, so compute it with
      `buildMwr(aggValues, aggFlows, aggDates)` (`returnColumns.ts:109`) at
      request time and read its last element the same way.
- [x] **Populate `annualizedReturn` + `annualizedReturnWithheldReason`** —
      `annualizedReturnWithheldReason(index, dates)` then
      `annualizedReturn(index, dates)` (`riskMetrics.ts:213` / `:177`), exactly
      as `:1305-1319` does, and percent as that line percentises it. §82.1 made
      `/merged`'s absence of these the reason the Overview tab could not be
      reused; without them the cumulative tab's TWR p.a. tile reads `—` forever.
      > **The withholding predicate is shared on purpose**
      > (`annualizedReturnWithheldReason` = ≥60 points AND ≥90 calendar days),
      > so the aggregate tile and the per-portfolio tile can never disagree about
      > the same window. Do not "helpfully" lower the floor for the aggregate:
      > it has more points than any single portfolio, so it is the side that
      > least needs the exemption.
      > **Unit trap, restated because this is a third call site:**
      > `annualizedReturn()` returns a **fraction**; `/:id/analytics` sends a
      > **percent** under the same field name, and `/:id/risk-metrics` sends the
      > fraction. §83.2 writes to the analytics shape, so percent it.
- [x] **`moneyWeightedReturnWithheldReason` mirrors `/:id/analytics`, which is
      hardcoded `null` (`:1545`).** `buildMwr` silently falls back to
      `buildSimple` when XIRR has no sign change (`:129-131`), so a value with
      `null` reason is not proof the number is an XIRR. Do not invent a new
      reason here — that would be a fourth answer. Record it as the same
      (accepted) defect the per-portfolio tab has, and let §83.2's test pin the
      *current* behaviour so the two tabs cannot diverge.
- [x] **Populate `monthlyReturns`** with `buildMonthlyReturns` (`:1294`) over the
      aggregate TWR index, so the Returns Chart is not empty — and, since §82.3
      landed, so the **Yearly** toggle has an index to walk. Yearly availability
      is still gated on `timeframe === "ALL"` in the SPA (`:467`); `/merged` must
      therefore honour `?timeframe=ALL` as the full window or the toggle shows a
      partial year as a whole one.
- [x] **Fix the early return at `:749-782`.** When *any* portfolio has fewer than
      2 snapshots, the route returns `backfillStatus:"pending"` with an **empty
      series** — so one brand-new portfolio erases every other portfolio's history
      from a view whose entire purpose is the cumulative total. Return the partial
      sum *and* the pending flag, keeping §72.7's rule that reporting a mid-rebuild
      portfolio is a read and firing a backfill from a GET is not.
- [x] Tests — a deposit into one of two portfolios must leave the aggregate TWR
      **unchanged** (§81.1's invariant, applied to the aggregate: this is the test
      that would have caught the missing `net_flow`); an internal transfer between
      two of the user's own portfolios leaves it unchanged; `Π(1 + monthlyReturns)`
      reconciles to `cumulativeTwr` at the last point; one portfolio with < 2
      snapshots still returns the other portfolios' series plus
      `backfillStatus:"pending"`.
- [x] Tests: `npm run test` green in `portfoliost-wallets`; `npm run build` (tsc) green.
- [x] Commit `feat(wallets): build the aggregate TWR and monthly returns in /merged`


> Landed in `portfoliost-wallets@31aed4b`: `/merged` now selects `net_flow`,
> `unpriced_value` and `carried_value`; `sumSnapshotsByDateForwardFilled` carries value
> and invested forward but counts flow only on its own date; `buildMergedPerformance`
> derives `cumulativeTwr` / `timeWeightedReturn` / `moneyWeightedReturn` /
> `simpleReturnPercent` / `annualizedReturn` (+ withheld reason) / `monthlyReturns` from
> `returnColumns.ts` + `riskMetrics.ts`, never from a stored column. `buildMonthlyReturns`
> MOVED from `routes/portfolios.ts` to `returnColumns.ts` so one month-boundary rule serves
> both routes. The pending early-return now returns the partial sum with the flag.
> 574 tests green, `tsc` clean.
>
> **Two boxes above were written before the code existed and needed widening, both
> recorded in the diff rather than worked around:**
> 1. The plan asked only for the two withheld *amounts*, but
>    `PortfolioPerformanceChart`'s chip needs a COUNT beside the amount —
>    `gapMessage` returns `""` when both `gapSymbols` and `heldGapSymbols` are
>    absent (`PortfolioPerformanceChart.vue:126-147`). Threading the amounts alone
>    would have left the honesty warning silent. `/merged` therefore also returns the
>    UNION of the per-portfolio `getGapSymbols` claims via a new `aggregateGapSymbols`
>    helper — a union, not a re-derivation, and `null` (not `[]`) when nothing claims
>    a gap, per §72.30.
> 2. `unpricedValue`/`carriedValue` had to become tri-state on the aggregate: a
>    contributor that did not measure them makes the whole sum `null` (unknown), not
>    a sum of the measured ones. Summing past an unmeasured row would report "nothing
>    withheld" on exactly the series that need the warning — the same argument the
>    per-portfolio route makes at `portfolios.ts:1272-1277`.

### 83.2 — `/merged`: sum the flows and build the aggregate return columns

The only step that makes the tab possible. Everything after it is presentation.

- [x] **Add `netFlow`, `unpricedValue` and `carriedValue`** to the `/merged`
      SELECT (`portfolios.ts:786-792`) and thread all three through
      `sumSnapshotsByDateForwardFilled` (`mergedAnalytics.ts:83`) so the aggregate
      sums them per date exactly as it already sums `value` / `invested`. A
      portfolio with no row on date *d* contributes its carried value and **0**
      flow, so its slice of that day's return is 0 — which is correct, not an
      omission.
      > The two withheld amounts are not optional. They are what fires
      > `PortfolioPerformanceChart`'s §78.5 chip (`:109-146`), which reports
      > *"up to 10,465 PLN is missing from this curve"*. Omitting them reuses a
      > chart component with its honesty warning silently disarmed — on the one
      > screen where a wrong total is most expensive. `unpricedValue` must stay
      > **absent rather than 0** on a row that predates the column, for the reason
      > the per-portfolio route spells out at `portfolios.ts:1268-1277`.
- [x] **Chain the aggregate TWR** through `buildDailyReturns` + `chainReturns`
      (`returnColumns.ts:43`, `:53`) — the same path `buildTwr` takes. Do not
      re-derive `Vₜ/(Vₜ₋₁+Fₜ)−1` here, and do not read any stored
      `cumulative_twr` column: those are per-portfolio and summing indices is
      meaningless.
- [x] **Emit per-point `cumulativeTwr`** on the aggregate series, and the scalars
      `timeWeightedReturn` / `moneyWeightedReturn` / `simpleReturnPercent` from
      the last index point, mirroring `:1381-1389`. The aggregate MWR has no
      stored `cumulative_mwr` column to read, so compute it with
      `buildMwr(aggValues, aggFlows, aggDates)` (`returnColumns.ts:109`) at
      request time and read its last element the same way.
- [x] **Populate `annualizedReturn` + `annualizedReturnWithheldReason`** —
      `annualizedReturnWithheldReason(index, dates)` then
      `annualizedReturn(index, dates)` (`riskMetrics.ts:213` / `:177`), exactly
      as `:1305-1319` does, and percent as that line percentises it. §82.1 made
      `/merged`'s absence of these the reason the Overview tab could not be
      reused; without them the cumulative tab's TWR p.a. tile reads `—` forever.
      > **The withholding predicate is shared on purpose**
      > (`annualizedReturnWithheldReason` = ≥60 points AND ≥90 calendar days),
      > so the aggregate tile and the per-portfolio tile can never disagree about
      > the same window. Do not "helpfully" lower the floor for the aggregate:
      > it has more points than any single portfolio, so it is the side that
      > least needs the exemption.
      > **Unit trap, restated because this is a third call site:**
      > `annualizedReturn()` returns a **fraction**; `/:id/analytics` sends a
      > **percent** under the same field name, and `/:id/risk-metrics` sends the
      > fraction. §83.2 writes to the analytics shape, so percent it.
- [x] **`moneyWeightedReturnWithheldReason` mirrors `/:id/analytics`, which is

- [x] **Populate `monthlyReturns`** with `buildMonthlyReturns` (`:1294`) over the

- [x] **Fix the early return at `:749-782`.** When *any* portfolio has fewer than

- [x] Tests — a deposit into one of two portfolios must leave the aggregate TWR

### 83.4 — Aggregate drawdown: no new route, no SPA arithmetic

Written this way because §81.1 made `computeRiskMetrics` **pure** — it takes
`(returns, dates)` and nothing else. After §83.2 the route already holds both.

- [x] **Populate the already-declared `performance.*` risk fields inline on
      `/merged`** — `maxDrawdown`, `sharpeRatio`, `sortinoRatio`, `calmarRatio`,
      `volatility`, `winRate` — by calling
      `computeRiskMetrics(buildDailyReturns(aggValues, aggFlows), aggDates)`
      (`riskMetrics.ts:242`). Every one of those keys is already declared
      (`openapi.yaml:1484-1491`), so this is wiring, not schema: **no
      `/merged/risk-metrics` route and no contract change.**
      > This is a deliberate transport divergence from the per-portfolio tab,
      > which reads `maxDrawdown` from a separate `/:id/risk-metrics` call. The
      > *numbers* come from the same `computeRiskMetrics`, so they cannot drift —
      > but do not hand-roll a second Max Drawdown in the SPA to "make it
      > symmetric". That is the drift this step exists to prevent.
      > **Units are the per-route ones, deliberately.** `computeRiskMetrics`
      > returns `annualizedReturn` as a **fraction** (that is what
      > `/:id/risk-metrics` ships), while `performance.*` on `/merged` is the
      > analytics shape, where `/:id/analytics` ships **percents** (`:1311-1319`).
      > So the one field this step writes twice — `annualizedReturn`, populated in
      > §83.2 — must be the analytics unit here too, and `maxDrawdown` /
      > `sharpeRatio` / `sortinoRatio` / `calmarRatio` / `volatility` / `winRate`
      > keep the ratios-as-fractions form the Risk tab already shows. Writing the
      > risk-metrics form onto `/merged` would put the same contract field at two
      > magnitudes on one response, which is the defect §82.1's comment records.
- [x] **Do not add a Max Drawdown tile to the aggregate tab** beyond the one the
      Drawdown card already renders. Per D89, risk *ratios* stay on the Risk tab;
      the aggregate has no Risk tab, so drawdown is the only one of these that
      travels, and it travels because the existing card needs it.

      `{100, 50, 150, 75}` reports **−75%**, not −50%, and

      `maxDrawdown` on the peak-to-trough leg.

## 85. Every ticker is a link to its research page (2026-10-02)

User request (no proposal file): *"Extend stock ticker to be clickable. Link
should lead to research page for this stock (bond, fund, etc)."* — and, on
follow-up, not only to add the missing links but to **put a `TickerBadge`
where a symbol is still rendered as plain text** (Top/Bottom Performers,
Dividend History, and the rest of that list).

**Half of this already exists and must not be rebuilt.** §60.1–60.3 established
the only sanctioned way into research — `researchRoute(symbol, route.fullPath)`
(`src/utils/research.ts:14`) plus the `from` query param and
`researchBackTarget` — and wired it at eight call sites. Four surfaces are
already linked: the transactions table (`:390`), the holdings table
(`PortfolioHoldingsTab.vue:417`), the calendar chips
(`PortfolioCalendarTab.vue:218`) and the compare rows
(`PortfolioCompareTab.vue:59`). §85 adds call sites to that same helper. It
introduces no new route, no new component, and no second way to build a link.

**The gap, measured.** An audit of every surface that shows a symbol found:

- **9 files render a `TickerBadge` that is not inside a link** —
  `TransactionFormFields.vue:59` (shared by the Add-Position stock step *and*
  `EditPositionDialog.vue:321`), `AddPositionDialog.vue:555`,
  `EditTransactionModal.vue:184`, `RecordDividendDialog.vue:124`,
  `PortfolioDividendsTab.vue:98`, `PortfolioNewsTab.vue:62`,
  `PortfolioPerformanceTab.vue:685` + `:708`, `ResearchCompare.vue:56`.
- **10 files render a symbol as bare text** — the chart-modal `<h2>`
  (`PortfolioHoldingsTab.vue:578`), the Edit-position (`EditPositionDialog.vue:278`)
  and Add-position (`AddPositionDialog.vue:507`) dialog headings, the yearly
  returns `vs {{ benchmarkSymbol }}` header (`:644`), both Chart-controls
  benchmark lists (`:757`, `:763`), the Charting page chip and comparison
  headers (`ChartingView.vue:130`, `:190`), the public share holdings table
  (`PublicPortfolioView.vue:72`), and the admin bond-catalogue / market-data
  symbol cells (`BondCatalogueView.vue:66`, `MarketDataView.vue:140`, `:187`,
  `:212`).

**Ordering: run §83 first.** §83.1 moves the Top/Bottom Performers block out of
`PortfolioPerformanceTab.vue` into `PerformanceTabContent.vue`. §85.2/§85.3 edit
those exact lines and the Chart-controls modal, so **apply them to
`PerformanceTabContent.vue`, not to the file §83.1 empties.** Doing §85 first
means doing the same four edits twice.

Recorded decisions (resolved with the user):

- **Mechanism: wrap the call site.** Add
  `<router-link :to="researchRoute(sym, route.fullPath)">` around the badge,
  exactly as `TransactionsTable.vue:390`, `PortfolioHoldingsTab.vue:417` and
  `WatchlistsView.vue:128` already do. **No `to` prop on `TickerBadge`** — it
  is documented as "fetches nothing" and each call site passes the data it has
  (`docs/COMPONENTS.md`), and a router-coupled prop breaks its no-router unit
  mounts. **No `TickerLink.vue` wrapper** either: 19 call sites do not justify a
  fourth layer, and the wrapping is the pattern §60.2 already proved.
- **Inside a modal, the badge does not use `router-link`.** `router-link`
  navigates without closing the dialog it sits in, leaving the research page
  under an unmounting overlay. Modal surfaces reuse the emit-then-push path
  those files already have (`EditTransactionModal.goResearch` `:162`,
  `AddPositionDialog.goResearch` `:463`, `PortfolioHoldingsTab.goResearch`
  `:313`) — `emit("close")` first, then
  `router.push(researchRoute(sym, route.fullPath))`. This is also why
  `from` is the page *behind* the modal: the route is unchanged while a modal
  is open.
- **Scope: everywhere, including the public share page and the admin tables.**
- **A symbol that has no research page stays clickable.** `/:symbol/profile`
  already falls back to the bond profile (`portfoliost-instruments/src/routes/instruments.ts:366-375`)
  and `ResearchOverview.vue:217` already renders a "Limited data availability"
  banner for a symbol with identity but no market data. Only a total 404 leaves
  the red error banner — that page is **left exactly as it is**, it is
  pre-existing behaviour and not this section's business.

Rules: one step = one commit; a step is marked `[x]` only after its tests pass
(unit + e2e against the dockerized stack per `AGENTS.md`).

### 85.1 — `researchBackTarget`: a second allowlisted internal prefix

The one prerequisite, and it is tiny. The share page lives at
`/public/portfolio/:shareId` (`router/index.ts:36-40`, `meta: { public: true }`),
and `researchBackTarget` (`:28-32`) accepts only a `from` starting `/en/` — so a
`from` passed from the share page would be **silently discarded** and "Go back"
would land on `/en/investments` instead of the share.

- [x] Accept two literal internal prefixes in `researchBackTarget`: `/en/` (as
      today) and `/public/`. Nothing else changes — no scheme, no `//`, no
      relative path can satisfy either, so the open-redirect property is
      identical to what §60.1 established.
      > Do **not** generalise this to "any path that starts with a slash".
      > `/logout` and the catch-all `/:pathMatch(.*)*` are both single-segment
      > or otherwise outside the two prefixes precisely so they cannot be used
      > as a redirect target. Two named prefixes is the whole allowlist.
      > `src/utils/research.ts` — `RESEARCH_BACK_PREFIXES = ["/en/", "/public/"]`,
      > matched with `.some(startsWith)`. Tests pin the lookalikes: `/publicsomething`,
      > `//public`, `/logout`, relative `public/…`, and the bare `"/en"` / `"/public"`
      > (no trailing slash) all still fall back.
- [x] Tests in `tests/unit/utils/research.test.ts`: `/public/portfolio/abc123`
      passes through; `/publicsomething`, `//public`, `http://…`, `public/…`
      (relative) and a non-string still fall back to `/en/investments` — the
      trailing-slash shape matters, so `"/en"` alone must still be rejected.
- [x] Tests: `npm run test` green.
      > 590/590 unit (71 files), 242/242 `test:mock`, `npm run build`
      > (vue-tsc + vite) clean. No `lint` script in this repo. The AbortError
      > lines in the vitest output are the pre-existing happy-dom teardown
      > noise, not failures.
      > e2e `tests/e2e/research.spec.ts` against the rebuilt docker stack:
      > 20 passed / 1 skipped — including all five §60.3 "Go back" tests, so
      > the existing `/en/` origins are unregressed.
- [x] Commit `feat(spa): let the research back link return to a shared portfolio`

## 86. Key facts per instrument class — bonds, funds, ETFs, crypto (2026-10-02)

User request (no proposal file): *"Make a specific 'key facts' in Research per
instrument. Currently it is designed for stocks, but we have bonds, funds, crypto
and they have their own specific information we currently miss, even different
bonds types has different info."*

**The gap, measured, not assumed.** The Key Facts card
(`ResearchOverview.vue:297-335`) is eight hard-coded `<dt>/<dd>` pairs — Name,
Sector, Industry, Country, ISIN, Exchange, Employees, CEO. Six of those are
shared identity; **Sector, Industry, Employees and CEO are equity-only**, and for
any non-equity symbol all four render a dash. Four of the eight are *already
fetched and thrown away at the last step*:

- **`etf_category` is populated and never displayed.** The profile route maps it
  into `finnhubIndustry` (`routes/instruments.ts:446`) and separately into
  `gicsSector` (`:447`); the card reads `gicsSector` for "Sector" and
  `gicsIndustry` for "Industry", and `translate.ts:221-224` hard-codes
  `gicsSector`/`gicsIndustryGroup`/`gicsIndustry`/`gicsSubIndustry` all `null`.
  Verified live in the local reference table: `etf_category` holds
  `"Equity"` / `"Fixed Income"` for 16 530 ETF rows. **The cheapest real win in
  this section is a row the backend already fills.**

**`toInstrumentProfile` is the lossy point, and it is lossy for every class.**
`translate.ts:189-231` reads only equity-shaped keys. For a savings bond the
provider returns ten fields and the translator emits three. For a Catalyst
corporate bond it returns thirteen and emits three. Verified live through
cachest on 2026-10-02:

```
GET :8090/fixedincome/profile/…  → upstream 404 (no emissions synced locally)
GET :8090/corp-bond/profile/BST0327
  {"symbol":"BST0327","name":"Best S.A.","isin":"PLBEST000333",
   "stock_exchange":"GPW RR","hq_country":"PL","asset_type":"corp_bond",
   "issuer":"Best S.A.","series":"W3","market":"GPW RR","status":"Notowane",
   "nominal_value":"100.0","nominal_currency":"PLN","secured":"NIE",
   "coupon_type":"zmienne WIBOR 3M + 4%","current_rate":"7.83%",
   "maturity_date":"2027-03-07","country":"PL","currency":"PLN"}
GET :8090/crypto/profile/BTC-USD
  {"symbol":"BTC-USD","currency":"USD","price":84127.1484,"date":"2026-10-02"}
```

Every one of those bond fields — issuer, series, coupon type, current rate,
maturity, secured, status, nominal — is **already in production through the
provider tier, is cached by cachest, and dies in the translator.**

**Two provider profiles are never called at all.** `src/adapters/cachest.ts` has
`fetchBondProfile` (`:138-140`, `/fixedincome/profile`) and has **no**
`fetchCorpBondProfile` and **no** `fetchCryptoProfile`, although both routes
already exist and are configured — `cachest/config.yaml:183-190`
(`OPENST_CORP_BOND_PROFILE`, `cache_ttl 86400`) and `:243-249`
(`OPENST_CRYPTO_PROFILE`, `cache_ttl 21600`), served from `openst/src/main.py:650`
and `:454`. Consequence, and it is a live bug rather than a missing feature: a
Catalyst bond symbol is not a savings bond, so `isSavingsBond` is false, the
profile route tries the **equity** tier (`:367`), and on failure tries the
**savings-bond** tier (`:456`) — which obligacje.pl does not carry. `/corp-bond/
profile` is never reached, so a Catalyst bond's research page 502s today. The
comment at `:371-375` documents the cost of the current probe order ("the equity
fallback spins through three OpenBB providers") and that cost is paid on every
bond lookup.

**The crypto ceiling is real and must not be papered over.** The installed
`openbb_fmp/models/crypto_search.py` declares `FMPCryptoSearchData` with exactly
`symbol`, `name`, `exchange`, `ico_date`, `circulating_supply`, `total_supply`,
and `openbb_core/.../crypto_search.py` adds nothing beyond `symbol` and `name`.
There is **no market cap, no rank, no ATH and no ATL** available from the one
configured provider (`openst/src/openbb_client.py:537`, `CRYPTO_SEARCH_PROVIDERS
= ["fmp"]`). Those four are recorded below as unavailable rather than specified
as nullable fields that are permanently `—`.

Recorded decisions (resolved with the user, 2026-10-02):

- **Contract shape: a nullable `keyFacts` on the existing `InstrumentProfile`,
  discriminated by `kind`, one schema per asset class.** Not a new route — the
  page already fetches the profile on every load (`ResearchOverview.vue:34-41`),
  so a second request buys nothing. Not flattened onto the profile either: at
  most six of ~20 flat nullable fields are ever populated for any one instrument,
  and the per-class rendering logic lands in the view regardless.
- **`kind` reuses the existing canonical vocabulary** —
  `stock | etf | fund | crypto | bond | corp_bond`, the exact `AssetType` union
  at `tickerref-queries.ts:8` and the lowercase form of the contract's six
  `InstrumentType` values (`translate.ts:86-108`). Six kinds, no seventh.
  `kind` is deliberately redundant with the existing `profile.assetType`: the
  latter is the contract enum in `SCREAMING_CASE` and is **nullable** when the
  symbol is absent from the local reference table (`routes/instruments.ts:429-448`),
  whereas `kind` is non-null whenever `keyFacts` is present and is what makes
  the union discriminable. A reviewer will ask why both exist; the answer is
  above, and it is the reason the two are not merged.
- **Bonds are two kinds, not one — `bond` and `corp_bond` — because the field
  sets are disjoint**, which is the request's own point ("even different bonds
  types has different info"). A savings bond has `rateRule` / `margin` /
  `redemptionFee` / `termMonths` / `seriesCode`; a Catalyst bond has `issuer` /
  `series` / `secured` / `status` / `couponType` / `currentRate` / `nominalValue`.
  They share only `maturityDate` and a notion of nominal, so they share one
  *concept* and nothing else — one schema with fourteen nullable fields would be
  worse than two schemas with six each, because every reader would have to know
  which half applies.
- **`margin` is not a contract field on either bond kind.** `CorporateBondProfileData`
  declares it (`corp_bond_profile.py:47`) but the scraper's own docstring says
  "`margin` is `None` — the detail page embeds the margin in `coupon_type` for
  variable-rate bonds" (`obligacje.py:62-68`), and the live payload above has no
  `margin` key. A field that is structurally always null is a permanent dash.
- **`margin` on a savings bond is a semantic overload and the card must not
  label it "Margin".** `_extract_margin` (`openst/src/importers/bond_series.py:228-246`)
  documents all three cases explicitly: for `rate_rule: "fixed"` the stored value
  *is* the flat annual rate; for `cpi_12m+margin` it is the inflation add-on; for
  `nbp_ref+margin` it is the NBP add-on. The column is called `margin` and means
  a **rate** in one case and a **spread** in the other two. The label switches on
  `rateRule` — see §86.9 — and the default label when `rateRule` is absent is
  "Rate".
- **Provider strings render verbatim; nothing is translated.** `secured` arrives
  as `"NIE"`, `status` as `"Notowane"`, `couponType` as
  `"zmienne WIBOR 3M + 4%"`. Translating them means inventing an English
  vocabulary the rest of the app does not have. One rule, applied once: raw text
  is shown raw, only numeric and date values are formatted.
- **Three Catalyst fields arrive as strings, not numbers, and two of them carry
  their own unit.** `nominal_value` is `"100.0"`, `current_rate` is `"7.83%"`
  (a trailing `%` that would render as `7.83%%` through `formatPercent`), and
  `secured` is a Polish boolean string. Each conversion is pinned in §86.6.
- **Crypto key facts are exactly what FMP returns** (user's call, after the
  measurement above): `name`, `exchange`, `icoDate`, `circulatingSupply`,
  `totalSupply`, plus the quote currency already on the profile. Market cap,
  rank, ATH and ATL are **not** specified as nullable fields — they are recorded
  as unavailable from the current provider, which is a different statement from
  "we fetch it and it happens to be empty".
- **Funds ship thin, on purpose** (user's call). The local reference carries
  name + aliases only; the ANALIZY snapshot CSV is
  `code,name,currency,points,first,last,close` (`openst/data/fund-catalogue.csv`,
  verified: `ARK01,Erste Akcji Polskich,PLN,7183,1998-04-02,2026-09-29,90.4`).
  There is no manager, category type, OPL/TER, risk class or recommended holding
  period anywhere in the stack. `FundKeyFacts` therefore carries **one** field,
  `categoryCode`, and the section says so on the page rather than implying
  coverage. The TFI detail importer that would fix it is named as follow-up in
  §86.10.
- **ETFs also ship thin**: `category` from `ticker_reference.etf_category`. That
  is one row, but it is a row the backend fills today and the UI discards.

Ordering: **contracts land before instruments, deliberately.** The provider-tier
rule (fixture → openst → cachest → instruments) orders *data*; the contract is a
*compile* dependency — `translate.ts` types its return as
`components["schemas"]["InstrumentProfile"]`, so an adapter cannot emit
`keyFacts` until the schema exists. Fixture capture still comes first, because it
decides which fields the contract declares. There is **no cachest step**: all
three profile routes are already configured, and the fix is on the instruments
side of the boundary.

Rules: one step = one commit; a step is marked `[x]` only after its tests pass
(unit + `docker compose` level per `openst/CLAUDE.md`, `cachest/CLAUDE.md`, and
`AGENTS.md`).

### 86.3 — openst: widen the crypto profile

`get_crypto_profile` (`openbb_client.py:610-626`) derives its body from the quote
and explicitly omits `name` because "name is not derivable from a price bar".
That reasoning was right for a quote-derived body and is now superseded: the
search leg already exists, already runs against the only provider that has
crypto metadata (`CRYPTO_SEARCH_PROVIDERS = ["fmp"]`, `:537`), and already
carries the name.

- [x] Rewrite `get_crypto_profile(pair)` to call
      `obb.crypto.search(pair, provider=<first provider with a key, honouring
      the existing `_provider_is_blocked` / `_provider_has_key` gate>)` and merge
      the matching row onto the quote-derived body. Add `name`, `exchange`,
      `ico_date`, `circulating_supply`, `total_supply`; keep `symbol`,
      `currency`, `price`, `date` exactly as they are.
      > **Match on symbol, not on the first row returned — and dash-normalise
      > first.** The fetcher's `transform_data` filters with
      > `str.contains(query, case=False)` and returns a list — `BTC` matches
      > `BTC-USD` but the first hit is not guaranteed to be the pair asked for.
      > Selecting `symbol == pair` and returning the body unchanged when there is
      > no exact match is the difference between a fact and a plausible-looking
      > wrong fact. §86.1 measured the sharper edge: FMP returns **`BTCUSD`**,
      > with no dash, and it is row **12 of 17** (row 1 is `TBTCUSD`, tBTC USD),
      > so a literal `symbol == "BTC-USD"` comparison matches nothing at all.
      > The comparison is against the pair with its dash removed.
- [x] `margin` is not part of this; it is not a crypto field.

      so a provider change degrades to `null` rather than throwing.
- [x] **Savings bond** (source keys from `openbb_client.py:727-738`):

      `maturityDate`←`maturity_date`, `termMonths`←`term_months`,
      `rateRule`←`rate_rule`, `margin`←`margin`, `redemptionFee`←`fee_b`,
      `nominal`←`nominal`.
      > `fee_b` and `nominal` arrive through `_plain`, i.e. as JSON numbers or
      > strings depending on the driver — `num()` handles both, and a
      > `termMonths` of `0` must survive as `0` rather than becoming `null`
      > (`num` already returns `0`; do not add a truthiness filter on top).
- [x] **Catalyst corporate bond** — the three string-shaped fields, pinned:
      - `nominalValue` ← `nominal_value` (`"100.0"`) →

      - `currentRate` ← `current_rate` (`"7.83%"`) → **strip the trailing `%`
        and parse the remainder**, yielding `7.83` as a number. Keeping the `%`
        in the value would render `7.83%%` through `formatPercent` in §86.9. If
        the string has no `%`, parse it as a plain decimal rather than
        returning `null` — `current_rate` is the single most useful number on
        the card and a missing suffix must not cost it.
      - `secured` ← `secured` (`"NIE"`) → kept as the provider's string. Per the
        recorded decisions it is **not** mapped to a boolean and **not**
        translated; `"NIE"` on the card is the honest rendering of a Polish
        source.

        `nominalCurrency`, `couponType`, `maturityDate`.
      > **`margin` is deliberately absent** — the scraper never sets it

### 86.8 — instruments: dispatch the profile by asset class

This is where the Catalyst-bond 502 is actually fixed, and it replaces a probe
order that costs a three-provider equity spin on every bond lookup.

      asset class **first** from the local reference via the existing

      provider profile: `bond` → `fetchBondProfile`, `corp_bond` →
      `fetchCorpBondProfile`, `crypto` → `fetchCryptoProfile`, everything else →
      `fetchProfile`.
      > Copy the pattern, do not invent one: `services/quote-dispatch.ts:109-121`
      > already dispatches the quote route exactly this way off the same
      > `assetTypeForSymbol` read, including the `catch` that falls back to
      > `"stock"`. Two dispatchers reading the same column is cheap; a third
      > ordering convention is not.
- [x] **Keep today's probe order for a symbol the reference does not know.** A
      null `assetType` means no sync has run, not that the symbol is an equity;
      falling back to the existing `fetchProfile` → `fetchBondProfile` cascade
      (`:453-464`) preserves current behaviour for unsynced symbols and is what
      stops this step from turning a WSE stock into a 404.
- [x] Leave the `/:symbol/detail` route (`:340-388`) on its existing path in
      this step. It has the same dispatch problem, but `InstrumentDetail` has
      not been given `keyFacts`, so there is nothing to fix there yet — noted
      here so the omission is deliberate and recorded, not forgotten.

      reference row with `asset_type: "corp_bond"` resolves through
      `fetchCorpBondProfile` and returns `kind: "corp_bond"` with `issuer`; a
      `BTC-USD` row with `asset_type: "crypto"` resolves through
      `fetchCryptoProfile`; an unknown symbol still resolves through the

- [x] Commit `fix(instruments): dispatch the profile route by asset class`
      > `aef1b87`. The Catalyst 502 is fixed and the regression is now a test: a
      > Catalyst bond whose **equity** profile succeeds with a plausible row is

      > incidental, and both were found by tests written from this step's own
      > examples:
      >
      > * `ticker_reference.listing_key` is now selected by `searchTickerReference`.
      >   The fund kind cannot tell an `ANALIZY::` listing from a `TFI::` one without

## 87. Withdrawal-on-sell, and a per-account "cash leg" switch (2026-10-02)

Owner-driven. Supersedes the `Wpłata`-row remedy proposed in §78.1: the owner
closed XTB with cash that never rests (deposit→buy, sell→withdraw), so the fix
is a **code path that already exists for buys and is missing for sells**, not a
new spreadsheet row per account.

**The asymmetry, measured in the code today.** `sheets-sync/src/transakcje-mapper.ts`
already posts an external cash leg for a funded trade — but only one direction of
it:

| sheet row | `Typ` | col 47 `wpłata/wypłata` | cash row posted | anchor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| any kontо | `Kupno` | `1` | `DEPOSIT`, `${externalId}#d` | `transakcje-mapper.ts:387-404` |
| `Equate+` only | `Sprzedaż` | `1` | `TRANSFER` → `IBKR`, `#t` | `:405-419`, gated on `SALE_PROCEEDS_TO` (`:23`) |
| every other kontо | `Sprzedaż` | `1` | **nothing** | `:411-413` — "the derived SELL +X IS the proceeds in place" |
| any kontо | `Wpłata`/`Wypłata` | `0` | — | parser **throws**, `transakcje-parser.ts:118-119` |

So a funded buy is a round trip (deposit nets the derived `BUY −notional` to ≈0)
and a funded sell is not (the derived `SELL +notional` credit stands alone with
no offsetting outflow). `invested` reads it exactly: `backfill.ts:1165-1168` —
"cumulative net EXTERNAL cash flow … deposits − withdrawals ± transfer legs",
position cost basis deliberately excluded. AU flags therefore decide whether a
portfolio has flows at all, and today a sell can never contribute one.

**Sheet state, measured read-only 2026-10-02** (spreadsheet
`1iDzR0OTHvqPbjjRSnAI4SdoD7sZOGy8uT9991sPFFps`, `Transakcje!A1:AU`, 2041 data
rows). `Sprzedaż` rows carrying `AU=1`:

| kontо | `Sprzedaż` `AU=1` | rows | `Wartość transakcji` | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Equate+` | 39 | — | — | already on the transfer path |
| `Rach. rejestrowy PKO BP` | 2 | 131, 132 | 8 500,00 PLN | inert today |
| `Crypto` | 3 | 317, 1180, 1181 | 39,33 USD + 113,40 EUR + 55,26 EUR | inert today |
| `IB` | 0 | — | — | settled 2026-10-02, see below |

All five inert rows read as deliberate — each is a sale whose cash left the
investment account, which is precisely what a `WITHDRAWAL` means. Contrast the
accounts that keep proceeds in place: `IKE Beata` 54 sells all `AU=0`,
`IKE Marek` 36 all `AU=0`.

**`IB` is a cash-holding account and stays out of this section.** The owner
normalised it on 2026-10-02: its 3 funded `Kupno` rows (1565, 1646, 1805 — all
ASR Nederland, 40 shares, 9 975,17 PLN / 2 344,88 EUR of `DEPOSIT`s that were
already being posted) went to `AU=0` alongside row 1852, the 40-share exit that
had been its matching withdrawal. `IB` now reads 387 `Kupno` / 91 `Sprzedaż` /
448 `Div` / 2 `Split`, **every trade at `AU=0`**, and its flows come only from 41
`Wpłata` + 5 `Wypłata` rows at `AU=1` — the explicit-deposit pattern, which is
the correct shape for an account that does hold cash. It is worth recording
because IB is the account that *looked* like XTB's twin: 3 funded buys in, one
full exit out. Had 1852 been left at `AU=1`, §87.1 would have closed it at 0 by
accident. It is deliberately the "proceeds stay put" case instead.

**Design decisions (resolved).**
- **A `Sprzedaż` row with `AU=1` posts a `WITHDRAWAL` **from the row's own
  portfolio**, in the row currency, amount `rowCcyCash(row)` — the same col 19 ÷
  col 21 helper the buy's `DEPOSIT` uses (`:100-104`). It is the exact mirror of
  `:396-404`, so a funded sell nets to ≈0 the way a funded buy already does.
- **For kontо on §87.3's list the cash leg is forced and `AU` is not consulted at
  all** — the owner's rule is "listed portfolios always force cash transactions to
  be created, not listed still check AU=0/1". This is what removes every
  spreadsheet edit from the section.
- `Equate+` keeps its `TRANSFER` → `IBKR` leg. The `SALE_PROCEEDS_TO` gate moves
  from "the only kontо that gets an outflow" to "the only kontо whose outflow is a
  transfer rather than a withdrawal", which is what it was modelling in the first
  place (`:40-54`).
- `AU=0` on a trade stays "pure replay, no cash row" (`:386`). Unchanged.
- New cash legs use the documented suffix convention `#d` / `#w` / `#t`
  (`:137`, `sync.ts:190`).

**Repos touched: three** — `portfoliost-sheets-sync` (the mapper),
`portfoliost-wallets` (the link + the cascade), `portfoliost` (the SPA setting).
Flagged here because it crosses more than two.

### 87.2 — 1:1 link between a trade and its cash leg

The two rows are created together and must die together. Nothing links them
today: `linked_tx_id` (`wallets/src/db/schema.ts:122`) is documented as the
cross-currency **transfer pair** link (`:100`) and carries no FK and no cascade,
and `transactions` has no cash column at all. The delete paths are
independent — `DELETE /:id/transactions/:txId` deletes only the trade
(`portfolio-transactions.ts:712`, delete at `:793`) and
`DELETE /cash/transactions/:txId` deletes only the cash row
(`portfolio-cash.ts:659`). Only the source wipe knows about both
(`import.ts:754`).

**Design decisions (resolved, owner 2026-10-02).**
- **A real FK, nullable, and it lives on the CASH row pointing at the TRADE** —
  `portfolio_cash_transactions.linked_trade_id uuid NULL REFERENCES
  portfolios.transactions(id)`. Not the other way round, and not by reusing
  `linked_tx_id`. The direction is what makes both deletes work with **zero
  application logic**:
  - delete the trade → the FK's `ON DELETE CASCADE` takes the cash row with it;
  - delete the cash row → the link dies with the row and the trade is untouched,
    because the link *was* the cash row.
  The reverse layout (`transactions.cash_tx_id`) would need hand-written cascade
  in `portfolio-transactions.ts:793` for the direction that matters most — silently
  orphaning a money row when someone deletes a trade — so it is the wrong end to
  put the key on.
- **Nullable, so it exists only when a related cash transaction exists.** `AU=0`
  trades, and every hand-written `Wpłata`/`Wypłata`, stay `NULL`. No row, no key,
  no sentinel.
- **Edits are explicitly out of scope.** Changing a funded trade's amount, price
  or date does **not** re-derive its cash row; the pair is allowed to drift.
  Accepted by the owner rather than solved — it is recorded here so the drift is a
  decision and not a bug report later.

- [x] `drizzle/0014_cash_leg_link.sql` — `ALTER TABLE
      portfolios.portfolio_cash_transactions ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS
      linked_trade_id uuid REFERENCES portfolios.transactions(id) ON DELETE
      CASCADE;` plus `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS
      portfolio_cash_transactions_linked_trade_id_idx ON
      portfolio_cash_transactions (linked_trade_id);` — **unqualified index name**,
      because PGlite rejects schema-qualified ones. Same file registers the column
      on `schema.ts`. Wallets runs `npm run db:migrate` as its container `CMD`, so
      the migration applies on the next rollout; `pfire-init-sql` needs no change
      (it carries only the `postgres_fdw` server and the `instruments.stooq_daily_*`
      foreign tables — zero wallets DDL).
- [x] **Backfill all 362 existing pairs.** The link is fully derivable from the
      `#d`/`#t` suffix convention: verified in PROD, `left(external_id,
      length(external_id)-2)` matches a trade for **362 of 362** suffixed cash rows
      (324 `#d` DEPOSIT + 38 `#t` TRANSFER), with 1 977 of 1 977 trades carrying an
      `external_id`. One `UPDATE … FROM` in the same migration. `linked_tx_id` is
      left alone — it is the cash↔cash transfer pair and means something else.
- [x] Set `linked_trade_id` at import time, in the same transaction as the insert,

- [x] Leave both delete handlers alone. `portfolio-transactions.ts:793` needs no

### 87.4 — XTB closes at 0, with no sheet edit

      Compare the two routes: the withdrawn `Wpłata` row would have pinned
      `invested` at `2 716,60` permanently (buys only — the `2 957,88` of sales
      and the `+241,28` realised were never in it), which is the offset §78.1 was
      written to remove. The sheet row 138 insertion point worked out for it is
      not needed either.
- [x] Assert XTB closes: external flow nets to ≈0 across 2022-02-11 → 2026-10-02
      and `invested` on the final snapshot is ≈0 rather than `2 716,60` or `0.00`
      for the wrong reason. Baseline captured 2026-10-02: 1 695 snapshots, every
      row `invested = 0.00`, opening net `−1.90`, total return `−24.08`, and the
      `9.49 → −4.04` day on 2022-02-17.
- [x] Then §78.5's verification applies to XTB unchanged and §78.6's

> **PROD 2026-10-02 — it closes, and the two assertions needed different units.**
> The account is genuinely flat: **0 open positions**, 4 closed, derived cash
> balance `−0.79` USD, and 10 cash rows (5 DEPOSIT `+656.45`, 5 WITHDRAWAL
> `−649.97`, all ten linked to their trade). External flow in the row currency
> nets to **`+6.48` USD** — 1.0% of what moved, the sheet's own col-19 rounding.
> Not ≈0 in the portfolio's base currency, and it should not be: **XTB's sheet
> rows are USD while its portfolio base is PLN**, so `invested` converts each leg
> at its own historical rate (USD/PLN ≈ 3.96 in Feb 2022 → ≈ 4.4 in Feb 2023). The
> PLN-equivalent net flow is therefore `−236.82`, which is what the last snapshot
> reads and what the header shows as `Total Invested −PLN 236.82`. That is an FX
> loss on the round trip, not a leak, and it is the honest number.
> So the assertion holds where it was written (row currency ≈0, nothing pinned at
> `2 716,60`, not `0.00` for the wrong reason) and the plan's currency was wrong.
> The baseline it quotes also holds: 1 695 snapshots, opening net `−1.90`.
>
> **§78.6's re-measure, and a new finding.** XTB now HAS a flow series, and
> `moneyWeightedReturn` reads **`+1 023 769.62%`** on the Performance tab while
> `TWR p.a.` reads a sane `+7.70%`. XIRR is meaningless here by construction: the
> account's whole point is that deposits and withdrawals cancel, so net invested
> is ≈0 (negative in base ccy) and there is no capital base to annualise against.
> §78.6's earlier `XTB +1166%` was incomplete flow history; this is a different
> artefact of the same field, and it will hit every account whose external flow
> nets near zero — which is exactly the set §87.3 put on the kontо list.
> `annualizedReturn` already has a withholding predicate (§81, the SHARED
> `annualizedReturnWithheldReason`); `moneyWeightedReturn` has none, and it needs
> the same guard on the net-flow basis. That is a §78.6 follow-up, not a §87 one.

### 87.5 — Per-account setting: "generate cash transaction on buy/sell" (UI only)

**Owner decision 2026-10-02: the setting is UI-only and never touches the import.**
Two independent mechanisms, deliberately:

- **Import** — hardcoded kontо list, §87.3. Listed → always a cash leg. Not listed
  → obey col 47. The spreadsheet's `AU` keeps its meaning for every account not on
  the list, so the sheet never lies about an account it governs.
- **UI** — a per-portfolio boolean. The transaction form pre-ticks the "also create
  a cash transaction" checkbox from it, so the box reflects what will actually
  happen; the user can still untick it per transaction.

- [x] `portfolios.portfolios` gains `cash_leg_on_trade boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT
      false`, plumbed through `@marx2/contracts` (published `1.6.62`; consumers pin
      `^1.6.62`), the wallets portfolio routes, and the SPA's portfolio settings
      form. Default `false` so no existing account changes behaviour on deploy.
- [x] Seed the default from §87.3's list for the seven listed kontо — otherwise the
      UI would show "no cash transaction" for XTB while the importer creates one
      anyway, which is the exact disagreement this setting exists to prevent.

> `src/routes/portfolios.ts`, with a pointer back to the mapper's `ALWAYS_CASH_LEG`
> — the duplication §87.3's fourth bullet accepted, not an oversight.
> The existing rows needed a **data** migration, not just a column default: the
> ten PROD portfolios predate the column, so the default alone would have left all
> of them unticked. `0015_cash_leg_on_trade.sql` therefore carries the DDL *and* a
> guarded `UPDATE … WHERE name = ANY(ARRAY[…7…])` (the §7b rule from
> `database-schema-migrations.md`: a schema change and its data move may share a
> file, separated by `--> statement-breakpoint`).

      and on submit creates the cash row through §87.2's `linked_trade_id`, so a

> Both write paths needed it, not one: the new-position path (`POST /:id/positions`,
> which is itself a BUY) and the buy/sell path (`POST /:id/transactions`). The flag
